qc-aligrithm-volatility-clustering-in-bi.abstract: Bitcoin's volatility does not mix randomly across time. High-vol periods follow high-vol periods, low-vol stretches extend themselves, and the transition probabilities are stable enough to build a forecast from. Borrego Roldán's 2024 study quantifies this with hourly and daily data from

bullets: Bitcoin volatility does not mix randomly across time
High-vol follows high-vol; low-vol stretches extend
Transition probabilities are stable enough to forecast from
Measured on both hourly and daily Bitcoin data
en.data: Hourly and daily Bitcoin data from Borrego Roldán's 2024 study; the abstract cuts off before the window.
en.method: Classify volatility regimes, estimate transition probabilities, forecast the next period's regime.
en.one_liner: Quantifies Bitcoin volatility regime persistence and turns it into a forecast.
en.relevance_why: Hourly and daily BTC bars are free from any exchange API, but no entry or exit rules are given, so building a strategy needs real design work.
en.takeaway: Size positions off the current volatility regime — cut exposure when the high-vol state persists.

bullets: 비트코인 변동성이 시간에 걸쳐 무작위로 섞이지 않는다
고변동 뒤엔 고변동, 저변동 뒤엔 저변동이 이어진다
국면 전환 확률이 안정적이라 예측 모형을 세울 수 있다
시간 단위와 일 단위 데이터를 함께 썼다
ko.data: Borrego Roldán의 2024년 연구가 쓴 비트코인 시간봉과 일봉 데이터다(초록에 구간이 잘려 있다)
ko.method: 변동성 국면을 나누고 국면 간 전환 확률을 추정해 다음 구간 변동성을 예측한다
ko.one_liner: 비트코인 변동성 군집을 국면 지속 확률로 수치화해 예측에 쓴다
ko.relevance_why: 비트코인 시간봉·일봉은 거래소 API로 공짜에 가깝게 받지만 진입·청산 규칙이 없어 전략화에 설계가 더 필요하다
ko.takeaway: 포지션 크기를 변동성 국면에 연동해 고변동 국면에서 노출을 줄이는 데 쓴다

qc-aligrithm-volatility-clustering-in-bi.title: Volatility Clustering in Bitcoin: Regime Persistence as a Forecast

qc-allocatesmartly-does-trading-taa-stra.abstract: Most Tactical Asset Allocation (TAA) strategies trade once per month. That’s by design. Short-term market movement is mostly noise, and trying to time every zig and zag is a fool’s errand. A unique feature of our platform is the ability to follow these monthly strategies on any day of the month.

bullets: Most TAA strategies trade once a month by design
Short-term moves are mostly noise, hard to time
Platform lets you run the same strategy on any day of the month
Tests whether higher trade frequency pays off
en.data: Abstract names no dataset or evaluation window.
en.method: Runs standard monthly TAA strategies while varying the trade day and rebalance frequency.
en.one_liner: Asks whether running monthly TAA strategies more frequently improves results.
en.relevance_why: The abstract gives no entry/exit rules to code directly, but the inputs are just daily ETF closes, so data is trivial to obtain.
en.takeaway: Useful for splitting a rebalance across multiple days to cut timing luck.

bullets: TAA 전략 대부분이 월말 하루에만 매매한다
단기 등락은 대부분 잡음이라 타이밍을 노리기 어렵다
월중 아무 날에나 같은 전략을 따라갈 수 있는 환경을 쓴다
매매 빈도를 올리는 게 득인지 실인지 검증한다
ko.data: 초록에 데이터셋과 검증 구간이 나오지 않는다.
ko.method: 월 1회 매매하는 TAA 전략을 매매일과 매매 빈도만 바꿔 비교한다.
ko.one_liner: 월 1회 리밸런싱 전략을 더 자주 돌리면 성과가 나아지는지 따진 글이다.
ko.relevance_why: TAA 전략 자체의 진입·청산 규칙이 초록에 없어 그대로 코딩할 수 없다. 다만 필요한 건 일별 ETF 종가뿐이라 데이터는 쉽게 구한다.
ko.takeaway: 리밸런싱 날짜를 여러 개로 쪼개 타이밍 운(timing luck)을 줄이는 데 참고할 만하다.

qc-allocatesmartly-does-trading-taa-stra.title: Does Trading TAA Strategies More Often Improve Performance?

qc-blog-sec-form-4-insider-trading-pytho.abstract: Form 4 looks unusually convenient for quantitative research. It is public, structured and tied to a regulatory deadline: in general, a reporting person must file by the end of the second business day after a reportable transaction. The SEC's Form 4 instructions state the rule and also show why

bullets: Tests whether insider filings carry tradable information
Anchors the event on the filing date, not the trade date
SEC allows two business days to file, creating a lag
Abstract reports no return numbers
en.data: SEC Form 4 filings from EDGAR; the abstract names no evaluation window.
en.method: Parses Form 4 filings in Python, then runs an event study around the filing date.
en.one_liner: Runs a filing-date event study on SEC Form 4 insider trades in Python.
en.relevance_why: Form 4 is free on EDGAR but needs heavy XML parsing and cleaning, and the abstract gives no entry rules or performance numbers.
en.takeaway: Time any insider-buying signal off the filing timestamp, since the trade date is stale by up to two days.

bullets: 내부자 거래 공시가 정말 알파를 주는지 확인한다
거래일이 아닌 신고일을 기준점으로 잡는다
SEC가 정한 2영업일 신고 마감이 시차를 만든다
초록만으로는 구체적 수익률 결과를 알 수 없다
ko.data: SEC EDGAR의 Form 4 공시 데이터를 쓰며, 검증 구간은 초록에 없다.
ko.method: Form 4 공시를 파이썬으로 수집해 신고일 기준 이벤트 스터디를 돌린다.
ko.one_liner: Form 4 내부자 거래 공시를 신고일 기준 이벤트 스터디로 분석한다.
ko.relevance_why: Form 4는 EDGAR에서 무료로 받지만 XML 파싱과 정제 부담이 크고, 초록에 매매 규칙이나 성과 수치가 없어 2점이다.
ko.takeaway: 내부자 매수 신호를 만들 때 거래일 대신 신고일을 기준으로 잡는 게 핵심이다.

qc-blog-sec-form-4-insider-trading-pytho.title: Form 4 Insider Trading in Python: A Filing-Date Event Study

qc-equibles-what-happens-after-congress-.abstract: The obvious rule is to buy what members of Congress buy and avoid, or short, what they sell. Across 17,859 investable common-stock disclosure events, that rule fails. One year after a disclosure became public, the typical purchase event trailed the S&P 500 by 5.36 percentage points and the

bullets: Tests the popular rule: buy what Congress buys
Studies 17,859 investable common-stock disclosure events
Purchases trail the S&P 500 by 5.36pp one year after disclosure
en.data: 17,859 investable common-stock disclosure events, each tracked for one year post-disclosure.
en.method: Event study measuring one-year excess return from the date each disclosure went public.
en.one_liner: Copying congressional stock purchases underperforms the S&P 500.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: disclosure data is free and public, but the abstract gives no sell-side numbers, universe filter, or rebalancing rule, so a tradable version needs real design work.
en.takeaway: Drop congressional-buy copying from the signal set, or test it as a fade.

bullets: 의원 따라 사기 전략이 정말 통하는지 검증한다
투자 가능한 보통주 공시 17,859건을 이벤트로 분석한다
공시 1년 뒤 매수 이벤트는 S&P 500을 5.36%p 하회한다
ko.data: 투자 가능한 보통주 공시 17,859건을 쓰고, 공시 후 1년을 평가 구간으로 잡는다.
ko.method: 공시 공개일을 기준으로 삼아 1년 초과수익을 재는 이벤트 스터디다.
ko.one_liner: 의회 의원 매매를 따라 사는 전략이 실패함을 보인다.
ko.relevance_why: 규칙 자체는 단순하나 초록에 매도 결과와 리밸런싱 규칙이 없고, 공시 데이터는 무료 공개라 확보는 쉽다.
ko.takeaway: 의원 매수 추종 시그널을 알파 소스에서 빼거나 역방향 근거로 쓴다.

qc-equibles-what-happens-after-congress-.title: What Happens After Congress Buys or Sells a Stock? Evidence...

qc-jonathankinlay-a-sharpe-of-2-1-from-n.abstract: I gave a research agent four years of prices with no predictable structure in them — none, by construction — and it came back with a long/short book, an in-sample Sharpe of 2.1, and a paragraph explaining the economics of an effect that does not exist. That is the measurement in this post. The

bullets: Agents surface alpha even where none exists
Feed four years of structureless synthetic prices
Agent returns a long/short book, in-sample Sharpe 2.1
It also wrote economics for a nonexistent effect
en.data: One synthetic four-year price set with predictability removed by construction.
en.method: Run a research agent on price series constructed to have no predictable structure, then read what it claims.
en.one_liner: An LLM research agent found a Sharpe 2.1 book in prices built to contain no signal.
en.relevance_why: No tradable rule here, but it fixes how you validate agent output; the data is self-generated, so availability is a non-issue.
en.takeaway: Add a null-data control run to any agentic research pipeline and record the Sharpe it invents.

bullets: 리서치 에이전트가 없는 알파도 찾아낸다는 문제
예측 구조를 일부러 제거한 4년치 가격을 입력
인-샘플 샤프 2.1의 롱숏 포트폴리오가 나왔다
에이전트는 없는 효과의 경제학 설명까지 붙였다
ko.data: 구조를 제거해 합성한 4년치 가격 데이터 한 벌이 전부다.
ko.method: 예측 가능한 구조가 없도록 만든 가격 시계열을 리서치 에이전트에 넣고 결과를 관찰했다.
ko.one_liner: 구조가 없는 가짜 가격에서 AI 에이전트가 샤프 2.1을 만들어냈다
ko.relevance_why: 직접 매매할 규칙은 없지만 검증 절차를 손볼 재료다. 데이터는 직접 합성하면 되니 확보 부담이 없다.
ko.takeaway: 에이전트 리서치 파이프라인에 널(null) 데이터 대조군을 넣어 샤프가 얼마나 나오는지 먼저 재두면 된다.

qc-jonathankinlay-a-sharpe-of-2-1-from-n.title: A Sharpe of 2.1 From Nothing: The Second Number Your Agent Doesn't Log

qc-miktul-dual-momentum-for-a-collapsing.abstract: Turkish savers have argued about the same question for decades: keep the money in a lira time deposit and collect the interest, or convert it to dollars and hold. The dilemma is common enough to have a household name — faiz mi, dolar mı?, “interest or dollars?” Both answers have had long

bullets: Targets the Turkish saver's 'interest or dollars?' dilemma
Switches between the two instead of picking one
Both choices had long winning stretches historically
Tests allocation rules under a collapsing currency
en.data: Turkish lira deposit rates and USD/TRY over a long history; the abstract names no window.
en.method: Dual momentum allocation across two assets: lira time deposits and long USD.
en.one_liner: Applies dual momentum to the lira-deposit versus dollar choice.
en.relevance_why: Deposit rates and FX rates are public and easy to source, but the abstract leaves lookback and rebalance parameters unspecified, so 4.
en.takeaway: A switching rule for cash versus hard currency in high-inflation markets.

bullets: 터키 저축자의 오랜 고민, '이자냐 달러냐'를 다룬다
둘 중 하나를 고르는 대신 모멘텀 규칙으로 갈아탄다
두 선택지 모두 오래 우세한 구간이 있었다
통화가 무너지는 환경에서 배분 규칙을 검증한다
ko.data: 터키 리라 예금 금리와 달러/리라 환율의 장기 시계열을 쓴다. 초록에 구체적 구간은 없다
ko.method: 리라 정기예금과 달러 보유를 후보로 놓고 듀얼 모멘텀(dual momentum) 방식으로 배분한다
ko.one_liner: 리라 예금과 달러 보유 중 무엇이 나은지 듀얼 모멘텀으로 답한다
ko.relevance_why: 예금 금리와 환율은 공개 데이터라 확보가 쉽고 규칙도 명확하지만 초록만으로는 룩백 기간 같은 파라미터를 알 수 없어 4점이다
ko.takeaway: 고인플레 통화권에서 현금성 자산과 달러 사이를 모멘텀으로 스위칭하는 규칙에 쓴다

qc-miktul-dual-momentum-for-a-collapsing.title: Dual Momentum for a Collapsing Currency

qc-papertoprofit-2x-your-portfolio-every.abstract: For those unaware, you generally make more money overnight than you do during the day when holding stocks. So much so that even if you just held the SPY overnight (buy at close, sell at market open the next day), you would net considerably more than if you held it during the day (buy at open, sell

bullets: Starts from the gap: stock gains cluster overnight, not intraday
Rule is mechanical — buy at the close, sell at the next open
Overnight SPY nets considerably more than the intraday leg
en.data: Daily SPY opens and closes; the abstract names no evaluation window.
en.method: Compare close-to-open SPY holding against open-to-close holding, then scale it up.
en.one_liner: The author amplifies the overnight effect: hold SPY from close to next open, not during the day.
en.relevance_why: Data is trivial — daily OHLC — but the abstract omits the leverage mechanism and universe rules behind the 2x claim, so it is not backtestable as written.
en.takeaway: Rebuild the overnight-versus-intraday split yourself and check whether it survives commissions and open/close slippage.

bullets: 주식 수익 대부분이 밤에 나온다는 관찰에서 출발한다
종가에 사서 다음날 시가에 파는 규칙을 쓴다
SPY 기준 밤 보유가 낮 보유보다 훨씬 앞선다
ko.data: SPY 일별 시가·종가를 쓰지만 초록에 검증 구간은 적혀 있지 않다.
ko.method: SPY를 종가에 사서 다음 개장가에 파는 오버나이트 보유를 낮 보유와 비교한다.
ko.one_liner: SPY 종가 매수·시가 매도가 낮 보유보다 낫다는 오버나이트 효과를 키운 글이다.
ko.relevance_why: 데이터는 시가·종가뿐이라 구하기 쉽지만 '2배'를 낸 레버리지 방식과 종목 선정 규칙이 초록에 없어 그대로 백테스트할 수 없다.
ko.takeaway: 종가·시가 데이터로 오버나이트 대 인트라데이 수익을 직접 재현해 보고 수수료와 슬리피지를 얹어 남는 게 있는지부터 확인한다.

qc-papertoprofit-2x-your-portfolio-every.title: 2x Your Portfolio Every Year: How I Turbocharged the Overnight Effect

qc-quanterlab-dalio-s-all-weather-constr.abstract: People usually take All Weather for the fixed allocation Dalio gave Tony Robbins, which is the one every retail article prints, but that one is All Seasons and it carries no borrowing at all. All Weather proper is risk parity borrowed up until the book carries a 60/40's volatility, which means

bullets: Retail 'All Weather' is really unlevered All Seasons
True version levers risk parity to 60/40 volatility
Benchmarks it against inverse vol, ERC, and 60/40
en.data: The abstract names no dataset or evaluation window.
en.method: Equalize risk contributions across sleeves, then borrow until portfolio vol matches a 60/40.
en.one_liner: Tests levered All Weather against inverse vol, ERC, and 60/40.
en.relevance_why: Rules are explicit and need only asset prices, which are easy to source, but financing cost and rebalance cadence are left to the implementer — hence 4.
en.takeaway: Use it as a vol-targeted leverage layer in a multi-asset allocator, run side by side with inverse vol and ERC.

bullets: 리테일이 아는 올웨더는 사실 무차입 올시즌스다
60/40 변동성에 맞춰 리스크 패리티를 차입한다
역변동성, ERC, 60/40을 같은 기준으로 비교한다
ko.data: 초록에 데이터셋과 검증 구간이 적혀 있지 않다
ko.method: 자산별 리스크 기여를 맞춘 뒤 60/40 변동성 수준까지 차입 비중을 올리는 방식이다
ko.one_liner: 레버리지를 건 올웨더를 역변동성, ERC, 60/40과 붙여 검증한다
ko.relevance_why: 규칙이 명확하고 필요한 값이 자산 가격뿐이라 데이터 확보가 쉽지만 차입 비용과 리밸런싱 주기는 직접 정해야 해서 4다.
ko.takeaway: 멀티에셋 배분 엔진에서 목표 변동성 기준 레버리지 층을 역변동성, ERC와 나란히 돌려볼 만하다

qc-quanterlab-dalio-s-all-weather-constr.title: All Weather built and tested against inverse vol, ERC and a 60/40

qc-quanterlab-dalio-s-holy-grail-measure.abstract: The most liquid fund shelf a person can buy holds 3.3 independent bets. Dalio's chart needs fifteen. The Holy Grail of investing, in his words: find fifteen good, uncorrelated return streams and risk falls by roughly eighty percent while return stands still. At correlation zero, fifteen equal

bullets: Dalio's chart needs 15 bets; the liquid shelf holds 3.3
Counts independent bets in buyable, most-liquid funds
At zero correlation, 15 streams cut risk about 80%
en.data: Most liquid retail-buyable fund shelf, 2008-2025.
en.method: Counts independent (uncorrelated) return streams and maps them to risk reduction.
en.one_liner: Tests Dalio's fifteen-uncorrelated-bets claim on a real fund shelf.
en.relevance_why: Listed fund prices are easy to source, but the paper gives no entry or exit rules, so allocation design is on you.
en.takeaway: Target independent bet count, not holding count, when sizing a multi-asset book.

bullets: 달리오 차트는 15개, 현실 펀드는 3.3개뿐이다
가장 유동성 좋은 펀드로 독립 베팅 수를 센다
상관 0이면 15개로 위험이 약 80% 준다
ko.data: 개인이 살 수 있는 유동성 상위 펀드, 2008~2025년 구간
ko.method: 무상관 수익원 개수(독립 베팅 수)를 세어 위험 감소폭을 따진다
ko.one_liner: 달리오의 15개 무상관 수익원 주장을 실제 ETF로 검증한다
ko.relevance_why: 데이터는 상장 ETF 가격이라 구하기 쉽지만 매매 규칙이 없어 배분 설계를 따로 해야 한다
ko.takeaway: 포트폴리오를 짤 때 종목 수 대신 독립 베팅 수를 목표로 잡는다

qc-quanterlab-dalio-s-holy-grail-measure.title: Dalio Holy Grail walked 2008-2025

qc-quanterlab-one-half-of-the-magic-form.abstract: Joel Greenblatt's Magic Formula ranks companies on two numbers and buys the ones that score well on both. One asks whether a business is cheap. The other asks whether it is any good. The claim in the book is that the pair works better than either number on its own. We tested that claim by

bullets: Greenblatt claims cheap plus good beats either half
Authors rank stocks on each metric separately
Quality-only ranking outperformed the combination
Adding the value leg dragged returns down
en.data: Abstract names no dataset or test window.
en.method: Rank stocks on earnings yield and return on capital separately, then race each against the combined rank.
en.one_liner: Splitting the Magic Formula in two, quality alone beat the combined rank.
en.relevance_why: Fully reproducible from public filings data, but the abstract leaves universe and rebalance cadence to you; +1 for refuting a popular retail strategy.
en.takeaway: Drop or down-weight the cheapness leg and screen on the quality metric alone.

With common beliefs, a risk-free asset and market clearing, the CAPM adds one decisive

qp-boundaries-of-time-series-momentum.abstract: Time-series momentum stands as one of the most reliable and heavily backtested anomalies in quantitative finance, serving as a foundational alpha source for modern managed futures and trend-following strategies. However, a recent academic paper by Matti Suominen and Erik Hjalmarsson, titled "Boundaries of Time Series Momentum," uncovers a structural vulnerability that every practitioner must account for. The authors demonstrate that while equity market trends persist reliably during normal business cycles, they systematically break down and aggressively reverse when market valuations reach historical extremes. This phenomenon establishes clear macro "boundaries" where chasing the trend shifts from a highly profitable strategy to a severe drawdown risk.

bullets: Practitioners treat trend following as an all-weather alpha
The authors split history by market valuation level
Equity trends persist in normal cycles, reverse at extremes
Result: a macro boundary that flips trend into drawdown risk
en.data: The abstract names no dataset or evaluation window.
en.method: Condition time-series momentum returns on the level of market valuation.
en.one_liner: Suominen and Hjalmarsson show time-series momentum fails at valuation extremes.
en.relevance_why: Valuation metrics and index prices are free and public, but you must set the thresholds and exit rules yourself.
en.takeaway: Use a valuation regime filter to cut equity trend exposure when valuations hit historical extremes.

qp-from-backtest-to-benchmark-validating.abstract: A profitable backtest is rarely the end of a research process. In professional quantitative research, the more important question often comes after the first positive result: is the strategy genuinely new, or is it simply another version of an already known factor, timing rule, or anomaly? This is especially relevant when a researcher develops a new systematic strategy with a clean historical equity curve. The strategy may have acceptable risk-adjusted performance, stable drawdowns, and a logical trading rule, but those statistics alone do not prove that the idea is unique. A silver strategy, for example, may look different on the surface while still behaving like a known commodity timing model, a trend-following strategy, a volatility filter, or a broader macro factor exposure. This article shows how Quantpedia API can be used as a benchmark dataset for validating new research. Instead of evaluating a new backtest in isolation, the strategy is compared against the Quantpedia universe of documented quantitative strategies. The workflow identifies nearest neighbours, assigns the strategy to a factor cluster, calculates a uniqueness score, and produces a research robustness report that can be used for deeper validation. The goal is not to replace human research judgment. The goal is to create a structured robustness checker that helps researchers understand whether a new strategy is truly differentiated, redundant with known effects, or simply a variation of an existing Quantpedia strategy profile.

bullets: A clean equity curve does not prove the idea is original
Compare the backtest to the Quantpedia strategy universe
Find nearest neighbours, assign a factor cluster, score uniqueness
Output a robustness report flagging redundancy
en.data: Quantpedia's universe of documented quant strategies; no evaluation window given.
en.method: Nearest-neighbour matching plus factor clustering over the Quantpedia strategy database.
en.one_liner: Quantpedia benchmarks a new strategy against documented ones to test whether it is actually new.
en.relevance_why: Scored 3 — it improves validation methodology, but the Quantpedia API is a paid subscription, so the benchmark data is not freely available.
en.takeaway: Run it as a gate before allocating: kill strategies that duplicate a known factor or timing rule.

qp-getting-the-target-right-in-return-pr.abstract: Recent interesting research from Cakici and Zaremba, highlights an often-overlooked aspect of machine learning for equity return prediction: the choice of prediction target. Rather than focusing on increasingly sophisticated model architectures or feature engineering, the authors show that how returns are represented during training has a much larger impact on predictive performance. In particular, models trained to predict stock ranks instead of raw return levels generate substantially stronger portfolio performance—roughly doubling both returns and Sharpe ratios in large-cap universes.

bullets: ML research chases architectures, not the prediction target
Cakici and Zaremba swap raw returns for cross-sectional ranks
Large-cap returns and Sharpe ratios roughly double
en.data: Equity universes including large caps; the abstract names no sample period or market.
en.method: Hold the model fixed and vary only the training label: raw return level versus cross-sectional rank.
en.one_liner: Training models on stock ranks beats training on raw returns.
en.relevance_why: Rank labels come free from price data, but you still build the model, universe and rebalancing rules yourself — hence 3.
en.takeaway: Relabel an existing return-prediction model with cross-sectional ranks and measure the portfolio gap.

qp-is-trend-still-your-friend-a-microstr.abstract: Trend following was one of the most persistent anomalies in finance for nearly two centuries, yet its performance deteriorated sharply after the 2008 financial crisis. An analysis of approximately 100 liquid futures contracts from 1995 to 2025 shows that this decline is highly selective. The decisive factor is not asset class, liquidity, market electronification, or strategy crowding, but volatility-normalized tick size. After 2008, trend-following profits collapsed almost entirely on small-tick contracts across all signal horizons, while remaining largely intact on large-tick contracts. This finding suggests that modern trend-following portfolios are fundamentally split into two distinct regimes governed by market microstructure rather than traditional asset classifications.

bullets: Trend following decayed sharply after the 2008 crisis
Tests ~100 liquid futures contracts, 1995-2025
Profits collapsed only on small-tick contracts
Microstructure, not asset class, splits the book
en.data: About 100 liquid futures contracts from 1995 to 2025.
en.method: Sort futures by tick size scaled by volatility, then compare trend profits across signal horizons.
en.one_liner: Volatility-normalized tick size explains where trend following died.
en.relevance_why: Futures prices and tick sizes are easy to source, but the paper gives a universe filter, not entry and exit rules.
en.takeaway: Split a trend book by volatility-normalized tick size and cut or downweight small-tick contracts.

qp-quantpedia-api-for-peer-group-strateg.abstract: A single backtest can show that strategy was profitable, but it does not always show whether the strategy was competitive. This is especially true for systematic futures strategies. A trend-following strategy can have a positive Sharpe ratio, a long live-like performance history, and a reasonable drawdown, but those numbers are difficult to interpret without a relevant comparison group. A broad equity index is often not the right benchmark for this type of strategy. A monthly rebalanced multi-asset futures strategy has a different objective, different risk profile, and different return drivers than a long-only stock index. A more useful question is whether the strategy performs well compared with other systematic trend-following futures strategies. This case study shows how the Quantpedia API can be used to build a custom peer group benchmark for strategy evaluation. The workflow has two steps. First, Quantpedia strategy metadata is used to screen and define a comparable peer group. Second, the historical equity curves of the selected strategies are downloaded, converted into daily returns, and aggregated into an equal-weighted peer group benchmark.

bullets: A broad equity index misprices futures strategy skill
Screen strategy metadata to define a comparable peer set
Stack peer equity curves into an equal-weighted benchmark
One backtest shows profit, not competitiveness

en.method: Screen Quantpedia strategy metadata, download peer equity curves, convert to daily returns, average equally.
en.one_liner: Quantpedia builds a peer-group benchmark to judge trend-following futures strategies.
en.relevance_why: The evaluation workflow is directly usable, but it rides on a paid Quantpedia API, so data access is the binding constraint.
en.takeaway: Benchmark your own CTA sleeve against similar systematic futures strategies instead of the S&P.

qp-sectoral-intramonth-momentum-cycle.abstract: We document a persistent intramonth momentum cycle in U.S. sector ETFs that yields meaningful risk-adjusted returns when properly sequenced. Using the nine original Select Sector SPDR ETFs and SPY as the market benchmark from December 1998 through June 2026, we show that trailing 252-day sector momentum generates a positive spread on the first trading day of the month—and then sharply reverses on days two and three. A third, independent leg of the cycle emerges in the window from ten to five trading days before month-end, consistent with the intramonth momentum cycle recently documented at the single-stock level by Nathan, Suominen and Tasa (2026). Stitching the three legs together into a single composite strategy delivers 5.99% annualized return at a 0.55 Sharpe ratio for the long-short variant, and 3.77% at 0.54 for the market-neutral variant—all while being invested fewer than half the trading days each month. Our contribution is twofold: we extend the calendar-anomaly literature from individual equities to sector-level portfolios, and we provide practitioners with a transparent, low-turnover framework that translates these academic patterns into actionable trade schedules.

bullets: Calendar-anomaly work stopped at single stocks
252-day momentum, traded only on set month days
Long-short returns 5.99% a year at 0.55 Sharpe
Market-neutral leg: 3.77% at 0.54 Sharpe
en.data: Nine Select Sector SPDR ETFs plus SPY, December 1998 through June 2026.
en.method: Rank sectors on trailing 252-day momentum, then flip direction across three intramonth windows.
en.one_liner: Quantpedia turns an intramonth momentum cycle in sector ETFs into a dated trade schedule.
en.relevance_why: Scores 5: daily ETF closes are free and public, and the entry and exit days are spelled out.
en.takeaway: Run momentum long day 1, reverse days 2-3, add the T-10 to T-5 month-end leg as a separate sleeve.

qp-why-average-strategy-performance-can-.abstract: Average strategy performance is one of the most common shortcuts in portfolio research. It gives the researcher a clean benchmark, a single reference line, and a simple way to compare one strategy against a broader group of similar strategies. In many cases, this is useful. But it can also be misleading. The problem is that an average hides dispersion. Two peer groups can have the same average return, but the internal structure of those groups can be completely different. In one year, nearly all strategies may behave similarly and cluster around the median. In another year, the same average may hide a wide spread between winners and losers. For portfolio construction, this distinction matters. This case study shows how Quantpedia API can be used to go beyond the average peer group return and measure yearly performance dispersion across a group of trend-following strategies. The goal is not only to ask how the average strategy performed, but also how different the individual strategies were from each other.

bullets: A peer-group average hides the spread inside the group
Same average, different winner-loser gaps year to year
Quantpedia API supplies the strategy set for dispersion math
Allocation decisions need dispersion next to the mean
en.data: Annual return series for a trend-following peer group from the Quantpedia API; the abstract names no specific evaluation window.
en.method: Pull a group of trend-following strategies and compute per-year dispersion of individual strategy returns around the group median.
en.one_liner: The study measures yearly return dispersion across a trend-following peer group instead of just its average.
en.relevance_why: Solid portfolio-construction diagnostic with no entry or exit rules, and the peer-group data requires a Quantpedia API subscription rather than public prices.
en.takeaway: Use it to check whether splitting capital across similar strategies actually diversifies, by tracking dispersion alongside the peer average.

ssrn-3070678.abstract: A growing body of literature argues that CEOs are irrationally overconfident. I find that the most commonly used measure of overconfidence, holding deep-in-the-money options, may be less of a behavioral bias than previously thought. CEOs who hold deep-in-the-money options make a substantial profit, consistently earning returns above the S\&P500 with significant Fama-French five-factor alphas. Previous literature has also shown that holding deep-in-the-money options is correlated with increased innovation. I find that the relationship does not seem to be causal.

ssrn-7355099.abstract: On August 10, 2026, Nvidia announced memoranda of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize over five hundred billion dollars of third-party capital through GPU-backed financing platforms. This paper argues that the structure introduces a category of risk that existing asset-backed securitisation theory does not formally address. I identify three conditions shared with the mortgage-backed securities market before 2008: correlated collateral values, unproven cash flow assumptions, and asymmetric incentives between originators and downstream debt holders. I then define two risk categories specific to technology asset-backed lending: Vendor-Circular Financing, which describes the structural conflict created when a manufacturer backstops credit facilities enabling purchases of its own products, and Innovation-Cycle Depreciation, which describes the systematic destruction of collateral value triggered by the vendor's own product roadmap. Secondary market data shows that H100 GPUs have lost approximately seventy-three percent of their 2023 value by mid-2026, providing preliminary empirical grounding for both risk categories.

bullets: $500bn GPU financing sits outside existing ABS theory
Shares three preconditions with pre-2008 MBS markets
Names Vendor-Circular Financing and Innovation-Cycle Depreciation
H100 GPUs lost ~73% of 2023 value by mid-2026

ssrn-7355943.abstract: Financial technology has reshaped the way capital is raised, invested, traded, and supervised. Innovations in electronic trading, algorithmic execution, digital advisory services, and distributed infrastructure have altered the structure of capital markets and the delivery of investment management services, while introducing new categories of operational, technological, and regulatory risk. This research examines financial technology as it applies to investment management and capital market services. It considers the FinTech ecosystem and its participants, the digital transformation of primary and secondary markets, the risk management and cybersecurity implications of technology adoption, the governance and internal control frameworks required to oversee it, and the contribution of financial technology to financial inclusion. The study concludes with an assessment of the developments expected to shape investment management and capital market infrastructure over the coming decade.

bullets: Maps the FinTech ecosystem and its participants
Covers digital shift in primary and secondary markets
Reviews cyber risk, governance, and internal controls
Closes with a decade-ahead outlook on infrastructure

en.takeaway: Use it as a checklist when auditing execution stack, vendor, and cyber risk controls.

ssrn-7356758.abstract: We document a large and robust pre-announcement drift in Japanese equity indices ahead of scheduled Bank of Japan (BOJ) monetary policy decisions: prices drift up steadily in the days before a meeting, peak immediately ahead of the decision, and do not continue afterward, earning an economically large and statistically significant excess return without elevated volatility. The drift is concentrated in meetings preceded by high ex-ante implied volatility. It is the Bank-of-Japan analog of the pre-FOMC drift of Lucca and Moench (2015), with a distinctive Japanese feature-variable announcement timing-that aids identification.

bullets: Tests whether the pre-FOMC drift shows up in Japan

ssrn-7363041.abstract: The Gravity paper claims a recovered growth rate—the arch—for an investor who holds a baseline allocation and exercises stored safety after damage. This paper tests that claim in simulation, discovers the structure underneath it, and proves what the simulation found. The arch is an exact long-run law. Under the bang-bang shortfall rule studied here, for baselines below the market the gap to the arch line is positive recurrent with a closed-form stationary law. The fraction of time spent at Kelly converges to (p^* = y_0/(2-y_0)), and mean log-growth converges to the arch. At the market seat, the stationary law disappears and the convergence becomes degenerate. At the 20- and 50-year horizons tested, the arch is kept by both the median and the dollar mean, but not yet by mean log-wealth: the remaining shortfall is a transient whose clock is computable. Against the natural skeptic—a static portfolio at twice the baseline, or at the best static seat for the same goal—the moving portfolio loses on growth and dispersion and wins on the one thing it was built for: the probability of keeping the line. It does so with less average exposure, and for a computable number of years: 67 at 30/70, 78 at 50/50, 91 at 70/30, and 122 at the market. The crossover boundary (T^*(y_0)) is exactly characterized—the static side in closed form and the moving side by an explicit Laplace transform—and evaluated numerically as a curve in years. What remains outside the theorem—which paths fall deep, and how deep, before the law asserts itself—is the price. The price is itself a finding: exact, at a price, over time, within limits.

bullets: Tests the Gravity paper's claimed recovered growth rate, the arch
Simulates the bang-bang shortfall rule, then proves the structure found
Time at Kelly converges to p* = y0/(2-y0); log-growth hits the arch
Edge over static portfolios lasts 67 years at 30/70, 122 at the market

en.takeaway: Use it as a switching rule for accounts that optimize probability of holding a target line, not growth.

ssrn-7363442.abstract: Attributing future systemic tail losses across assets remains dominated by exposures estimated asset by asset, market beta, downside beta and volatility, although drawdowns are precisely the episodes in which losses become collective and concentrate where shocks recirculate among tightly co-moving names. The quantities proposed here originate in our prior work on network fragility: the FSRI, a structural index for microbial co-occurrence networks in agricultural soils, and its financial descendant, the TSI, whose standalone version we falsified and reported. From that starting point we hypothesized that the same structural information could carry marginal value if localized to individual assets, extended with a response dimension, and handed to a flexible learner as features rather than composed by hand. The result is the Omega Block: five per-asset features computed from daily prices alone, two triadic quantities measured against a closed-form configuration null and three response quantities around scheduled FOMC announcements, among them Omega-R, a perturbation response normalized by each asset's own baseline drift, developed for this block. In pre-registered paired ablations with a same-width noise placebo, the block adds 1.3 to 3.4 points of out-of-fold R 2 to next-year tail-loss attribution over baselines that instantiate the public state of the art, up to 31 columns including sector, downside beta, co-moments, a conditional MES proxy, size, liquidity and balance-sheet fundamentals, replicated on two universes and two nearly disjoint periods (2012-2017, 2016-2025), while the placebo worsens the same model in every configuration. Because the baselines that decide adoption in practice are proprietary, the paper's verification is designed to travel to the data: an open acceptance harness reruns the entire protocol on any universe, baseline and event calendar, with a values-only mode and a cryptographic time-lock. The scope established by the evidence is cross-sectional attribution, not market timing.

bullets: Downside beta and MES miss where shocks recirculate among peers
Two triadic features vs a null, three FOMC response features
Beats up to 31-column baselines by 1.3-3.4 points of out-of-fold R²

en.takeaway: Bolt onto a risk model to rank next-year tail-loss exposure and trim crowded, tightly co-moving names.

ssrn-7363443.abstract: We survey 28 leading Swiss pension fund consultants and asset managers to understand the factors and their ranking driving institutional asset allocation decisions. The risk tolerance of pension fund boards, target returns, and risk-free rates emerge as the most influential factors, while traditional portfolio theory predictors such as expected returns, volatility or individual risk aversion show limited practical relevance. Finally, we find that individual risk aversion of beneficiaries plays a limited role. Our findings suggest that while institutional investors may overcome individual suboptimal asset allocation choices, they face distinct institutional frictions that also influence asset allocation decisions.

ssrn-7363482.abstract: Buying an asset immediately after a large single day decline is one of the oldest ideas in short horizon trading, and it is easy to make it look profitable. This paper applies one event definition and one testing protocol to two asset classes, four US equity indices over seventy six years and, in results carried over from an earlier stage of the same research program, twenty cryptocurrency perpetual futures, and finds that almost all of the apparent effect is an artifact of how the events are counted. Large declines arrive on the same few calendar dates across instruments, so an event study that treats each instrument day as an independent observation is counting one market wide shock many times. In a panel of twenty eight single names, 1,361 declines at or below seven percent are only 791 distinct dates, and the pooled t statistic of 6.76 falls to 1.68 when each date is counted once. Three further corrections matter and are usually skipped: the depth thresholds that define such events are nested rather than independent, so a strong tail leaks into every shallower cut; testing several depths requires a familywise correction; and a stationary block bootstrap with a block length that is a large fraction of the sample is badly anti conservative, which in our own first pass manufactured a p value two orders of magnitude too small. After all four corrections, exactly one result survives in equities. Index declines at or below seven percent, 50 events on 25 dates clustering into 10 episodes since 1950, are followed by a mean next session return of 3.08 percent, with a familywise p value of 0.006 and a bootstrap interval from 1.34 to 4.84 percent. It is not crash window drift: the next session returns 3.08 percent while each of the following nine averages 0.01 percent, below the unconditional daily mean. It is implementable, since 83 percent of the move occurs after the opening print. Everything shallower is indistinguishable from zero, and the corresponding single name effect is absent. In crypto perpetuals the same mechanism fails completely, with an edge net of market beta that is negative in every regime and every year of a six year sample. The economics are the final constraint: an account trading the surviving tail signal deploys 0.05 percent of its capital time and beats Treasury bills by 0.44 points a year, which is a real effect that cannot carry a portfolio.

journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Event studies double-count one shock across instruments

en.data: Four US equity indices over 76 years, a 28-name panel, and 20 crypto perpetual futures over six years.

en.takeaway: Buy the index at the close after a 7% or worse drop, exit next session, and size it as a rare overlay.

ssrn-7365578.abstract: When an AI system appears to generate equity alpha, five explanations compete with genuine skill: factor exposure, a weak benchmark, data leakage, model complexity, and an advantage a conventional system could replicate. We test all five on the same signal. Using the peer-reviewed replication of 212 published anomalies, language-model and agentic arms forecast which anomalies persist after their original samples end. The arms earn significant factor alpha-and none of it survives comparison with a passive portfolio of all published anomalies, which requires no model at all. Leakage does not explain the result: contamination made performance worse. The models' verbal mechanism judgements outperform their own numeric scores, but in-sample persistence absorbs them. A composite forecast scoring 0.400 owes 98.5% of that to a statistic we supplied. Apparent AI alpha here is a benchmarking artefact, not information.

bullets: Five rivals to skill explain apparent AI alpha
LLM and agentic arms forecast anomaly persistence
Factor alpha dies against a passive all-anomaly portfolio
A supplied statistic drives 98.5% of the 0.400 score

en.takeaway: Benchmark any AI stock signal against an equal-weight basket of all published anomalies before believing it.

ssrn-7365579.abstract: Investment banking, shadow banking, and high-frequency trading are among those manifestations of modern finance that evoke fascination and mistrust in equal measure. Drawing on the academic literature and on current data from international institutions (Financial Stability Board, ESMA, SEC, LSEG), this paper examines what these lines of business actually are, how they function, who conducts them, and whose interests they serve. The analysis shows that all of the activities examined constitute legal, economically well-founded, and in large part regulated businesses whose questionable reputation stems chiefly from opacity, conflicts of interest, and isolated excesses. Investment banking is a highly concentrated business of a few large banks, with worldwide fee income of $60.5 billion in the first half of 2025 alone. Shadow banking, as recorded by the Financial Stability Board, comprises assets of $256.8 trillion and thus already 51 per cent of the global financial system. In high-frequency trading, roughly 55 per cent of US and up to 43 per cent of European equity trading volume is attributable to strategies whose reaction times are measured in millionths of a second; the costs associated with latency arbitrage amount to roughly five billion dollars per year worldwide (Aquilina, Budish, and O'Neill, 2022). For investors, a differentiated assessment follows: none of the businesses examined is disreputable per se, and none is free of risk. Those who understand how they work, who the participants are, and where the profits originate can weigh opportunities and dangers realistically — and may, in selected cases, participate in these markets themselves, whether through listed trading firms or through regulated credit funds.

ssrn-7365822.abstract: Satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated (e.g., China's Micius satellite) as a means of extending quantum-secured communication beyond fiber-optic range, with direct relevance to naval fleet communications and aircraft-to-base communications where mobile assets cannot rely on fixed fiber infrastructure. Unlike this research group's companion terrestrial BB84 study, which evaluated eavesdropper detection under near-ideal channel conditions, satellite links are dominated by a different physical effect: atmospheric photon loss, driven by slant-path absorption, scattering, beam divergence, and elevation-angle-dependent atmospheric thickness. This study models that effect using PKTron's density-matrix simulator, explicitly separating two physically distinct phenomena that are frequently conflated in simplified models: heralded photon loss (which reduces raw key rate without directly causing bit errors) and detector dark counts (a roughly constant background click rate that becomes proportionally significant, and increasingly drives quantum bit error rate, QBER, as the real signal weakens). Across four simulated transmittance scenarios representing satellite pass geometries from zenith (η=0.50) to near-horizon (η=0.005), sifted key count fell from 547 to 15 bits per 2,000 transmitted qubits, while QBER rose from 2.6% to 33.3%, driven by dark counts constituting an increasing fraction (1.3% to 60.0%) of all detector clicks. Hardware validation was performed on IBM Quantum's ibm_marrakesh processor for the surviving-photon measurement step, using the same classical channel model to determine which photons survived transmission. At η=0.50, hardware measurement yielded a 0.550 click rate (matching theoretical prediction) with 12 sifted bits and 0.000 QBER; at η=0.03, a larger sample (400 transmitted qubits) yielded a 0.037 click rate (again matching prediction) with 8 sifted bits and a QBER of 0.125, consistent with the simulated prediction of elevated error rates at low transmittance. These results confirm, in both simulation and on real quantum hardware, that atmospheric loss degrades satellite QKD primarily through reduced key rate and a distinct, gradual, dark-count-driven QBER increase-qualitatively different from the sharp, immediate QBER signature of eavesdropping demonstrated in this group's companion terrestrial QKD study-a distinction with direct relevance to link budget engineering for naval and airborne quantum-secured communication systems.

ssrn-7365979.abstract: This article examines three structural crises that the nation-state confronts simultaneously in the twenty-first century: demographic ageing and the unsustainability of social security systems; labour-market transformation driven by automation and artificial intelligence; and climate-induced food insecurity and migration. Drawing on recent institutional and academic literature (2018-2026), the study argues that these crises are not merely concurrent but mutually reinforcing through feedback loops that generate a spiral, placing the classical nation-state / welfare-state model under a performance-legitimacy crisis. The article proposes a four-layer model of "regulatory stakeholder capitalism" that moves beyond voluntary stakeholder capitalism by incorporating a state-capacity filter, SME proportionality, regulatory-arbitrage safeguards, and an inter-stakeholder prioritisation mechanism. Prepared as a descriptive-critical literature review, the paper advances five testable hypotheses and outlines a three-stage research programme intended to ground future quantitative inquiry. The contribution lies in integrating demographic-fiscal, technological and climatic pressures into a single institutional-response framework that treats state capacity as a central filter rather than a residual variable.

ssrn-7366094.abstract: We provide novel evidence on how investor attention interacts with corporate disclosure during the “full-consignment” shift in cross-border e-commerce, a reversal of the decade-long platform migration toward agency selling. Using 41,236 question-and-answer dialogues from China’s regulated investor interaction platforms for 118 listed supply-chain firms over 2022–2024, we document three counterintuitive findings. Consignment-related Q&A spikes generate overpricing that is larger and reverses faster than that associated with unregulated attention proxies: a five-day abnormal return of +2.9% fully reverses within six weeks, consistent with a credibility illusion created by exchange supervision. Attention also runs backward—investor questioning induces consignment narratives, concentrated in firms that never report consignment revenue. Finally, the market rewards narrative adopters while underreacting to genuine converters. The price-formation benefits of regulated interaction platforms are thus topic-contingent, and investor questioning constitutes a novel demand-side trigger of catering disclosure.​

ssrn-7366218.abstract: We examine whether NSE index derivatives exhibit a liquidity discontinuity at 15:00 IST, tied to mandatory broker RMS auto-square-off and, historically, the 15:00-15:30 IST closing-price VWAP window. Using kernel-density clustering, regression discontinuity design, and panel GMM on real Nifty 50 (2017) and Bank Nifty (2015-2026) minute data, plus a fully re-derived 62-stock cross-section, we find significantly elevated volatility-not directional returns-at 15:00-15:15, roughly twice as large for high-retailleverage stocks. Placebo tests at nearby cutoffs are also frequently significant, indicating an accelerating volatility curve into the close rather than a sharp, uniquely localized discontinuity.

ssrn-7366638.abstract: Climate policy uncertainty has become an important consideration for strategic asset allocation, particularly for long-horizon institutional investors whose portfolios are exposed to regulatory shifts and policy reversals. This paper examines how institutional investors can translate climate policy uncertainty into implementable strategic asset-allocation rules. Motivated by the distinction between risk and Knightian ambiguity, we use climate policy uncertainty as an observable state variable that governs the strength of portfolio shrinkage. Building on this idea, we propose two allocation rules. The first is an ambiguity-penalized robust mean -variance optimizer (ARMVO), which blends the maximum-Sharpe and minimum-variance portfolios with a blending intensity controlled by the uncertainty state. The second is an ambiguity-linked Black-Litterman model (ALBL), which shrinks the expected-return input toward the reverse-optimization equilibrium return using the same state variable. We implement the two rules using a rolling percentile of the newly developed climate policy uncertainty (CPU) index of f Gavriilidis et al. (2026) and test them on eleven global ETFs from 2012 to 2024. ALBL improves the Sharpe ratio from 0.119 for equal weighting to 0.286 and generates a certainty equivalent gain of 208 basis points per year for a risk-aversion parameter of γ=5, although the Sharpe-ratio improvement is not statistically significant at conventional levels. Asset-based attribution suggests that the improvement is not fully explained by a static allocation to the same ETFs. The paper contributes a transparent and implementable framework for ambiguity-aware strategic asset allocation.

bullets: Long-horizon investors lack rules for policy-reversal risk
CPU index acts as an observable ambiguity state variable
ALBL lifts Sharpe from 0.119 to 0.286 vs equal weight
Sharpe gain is not statistically significant

en.method: Two rules: ARMVO blends max-Sharpe and min-variance; ALBL shrinks expected returns toward equilibrium.
en.one_liner: The authors let a climate policy uncertainty index set portfolio shrinkage strength.
en.relevance_why: CPU index and ETF prices are public and easy to source, but this is a portfolio-construction technique, not a signal, and the Sharpe gain lacks significance.
en.takeaway: Use it as an allocation overlay where a macro uncertainty percentile dials shrinkage up or down.

ssrn-7367038.abstract: Background: Cryptocurrency is a digital decentralized currency that enables peer-to-peer transactions without the involvement of intermediaries, using blockchain technology to ensure security and transparency. These emotions can help understand when and what behavioral intentions toward cryptocurrency adoption are necessary. These insights contribute to the growing literature on fintech adoption in emerging economies and provide valuable guidance for policymakers and investors formulating cryptocurrency regulations in Nepal. Objectives: It aims to investigate the influence of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, and perceived risk constructs attached to an individual's intention to be involved in cryptocurrency transactions. It finally aims to study the relationships among these variables and their effect on cryptocurrency adoption in the Nepal context. Methods: The study uses a quantitative descriptive design and snowball sampling alone to extract information from cryptocurrency users in Nepal. A structured online questionnaire was used to gather 272 responses and analyzed using correlation and regression to investigate the significance of the proposed hypotheses. Results: Findings show that perceived usefulness, ease, or trust significantly and positively influence behavioral intention toward cryptocurrency adoption, while perceived risk harms adoption because users worry about market volatility, regulatory uncertainty, and security threats. Despite the government's legal restrictions, many Nepalese citizens are still involved in cryptocurrency transactions, seeing it as a source of financial benefit and investment opportunity. Conclusion: The study attests that perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust motivate behavior toward adopting cryptocurrency, while perceived risk provides a barrier. This enlightens policymakers on balanced regulatory measures that address risks while encouraging innovation in digital finance. These findings would provide valuable implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and technology developers in outlining the future of cryptocurrency regulation and adoption strategies.

journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

en.method: Tests TAM constructs — usefulness, ease of use, trust, risk — via correlation and regression.
en.one_liner: Surveys 272 Nepali crypto users on what drives their intent to transact.
en.relevance_why: Survey data cannot be reproduced and no trading rule exists, so there is nothing to automate.
en.takeaway: At most, colour for a view that crypto demand in ban-regime countries persists off-exchange.

ko.takeaway: 규제 국가의 암호화폐 수요가 금지에도 살아남는다는 정성 배경 정보 정도로만 쓴다.

ssrn-7367038.title: Behavioral Intentions Toward Cryptocurrency Transactions: Exploring Through Snowball Sampling Among Users

ssrn-7367160.abstract: This paper examines whether vocal delivery during Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) press-conference Q&A sessions contains market-relevant information beyond the words spoken. Using WavLM, a large-scale speech processing model, we construct a vocal-based measure of monetary-policy stance, defined as hawkish versus dovish rather than generic emotion, applied to 89 press conferences from 2011 to 2025. For each sentence, we compare the original human audio with a text-to-speech (TTS) rendering of the same text. The Human-TTS difference provides a fixed-text measure of Q&A delivery and speaker composition. Larger gaps are associated with higher short-window cumulative abnormal returns on Treasury ETFs across maturities, conditional on textual stance, macroeconomic conditions, monetary-policy surprises, and chair regimes. When economic policy uncertainty is high, larger gaps are also associated with higher S&P 500 ETF returns and declines in VIX and VVIX. The evidence indicates that the vocal delivery and speaker composition of the Q&A contain state-dependent information not captured by text alone.
ssrn-7367160.affiliations: National Taipei University, and National Taipei University

bullets: Asks whether delivery carries information the transcript misses
Compares human audio against TTS of the identical text
Bigger Human-TTS gaps predict higher short-window Treasury ETF CARs
Under high policy uncertainty, S&P 500 rises and VIX/VVIX fall
en.data: 89 FOMC press conferences from 2011 to 2025, matched to Treasury ETFs across maturities, an S&P 500 ETF, VIX and VVIX.
en.method: WavLM embeddings score each sentence on a hawkish-dovish axis; the human-minus-TTS difference holds the text fixed.
en.one_liner: The authors extract a hawkish-dovish signal from FOMC press-conference voices and link it to Treasury ETF returns.
en.relevance_why: The Fed posts the recordings, but sentence alignment, TTS rendering and WavLM inference are all on you, and the signal fires only eight times a year.
en.takeaway: Trade Treasury ETF direction in the minutes after the Q&A, sized up when EPU is high — if you build the audio pipeline yourself.

bullets: 발언 내용 말고 말투에도 정보가 있는지 물었다
같은 문장을 사람 음성과 TTS로 만들어 차이를 쟀다
차이가 클수록 만기별 국채 ETF 단기 CAR이 높았다
정책 불확실성이 높을 때는 S&P500이 오르고 VIX·VVIX가 내렸다
ko.data: 2011년부터 2025년까지 FOMC 기자회견 89회 녹음과 국채·S&P500 ETF, VIX, VVIX를 썼다.
ko.method: 음성 모델 WavLM으로 문장별 임베딩을 만들고 사람 음성과 TTS 음성의 차이를 매파-비둘기파 축의 지표로 삼았다.
ko.one_liner: FOMC 기자회견 목소리에서 매파/비둘기파 신호를 뽑아 채권 ETF 수익률과 연결했다.
ko.relevance_why: 회의 녹음 자체는 연준이 공개하지만 문장 단위 정렬과 TTS 생성, WavLM 임베딩까지 손수 만들어야 해서 데이터 확보 부담이 크고 규칙도 이벤트 하나에 묶여 있다.
ko.takeaway: 기자회견 Q&A 직후 몇 분 구간에서 국채 ETF 방향을 잡는 이벤트 트레이드에 쓸 만하다. 다만 음성 파이프라인을 직접 만들어야 한다.

ssrn-7367160.title: Hawkish by Voice: Financial Market Reactions to FOMC Communication

ssrn-7367199.abstract: We test whether ensemble machine-learning models can produce economically meaningful forecasts for daily S&P 500 returns over January 2000-May 2024 (6,266 trading days; CRSP). Eight technical predictors are engineered to capture momentum and volatility structure. A Random Forest (200 trees) and Gradient Boosting regressor (400 stages) are trained on 2000-2019 and combined in a convex ensemble (60% RF, 40% GB). On the 2020-2024 hold-out sample, the ensemble improves MAE by 3% versus its constituents but fails to beat a naïve zero-return benchmark in out-of-sample R 2. A long-only rule that takes positions only when forecasts are positive reduces drawdown and annualised volatility yet delivers only 2.1% CAGR, suggesting limited net value after trading costs. Importance analysis shows MACD and 21-day volatility contribute 39% of the predictive signal, and year-by-year errors confirm strong regime dependence, especially during the COVID-19 crash and the 2022 inflation sell-off. We conclude that tree ensembles aid risk control, but consistent performance likely requires regime-aware or deep sequence approaches with macro-sentiment features.
ssrn-7367199.affiliations: Westcliff University, International American University (IAU), , Westcliff University, International American University (IAU), Trine University, International American University (IAU), Ohio University and Westcliff University

bullets: Tests whether technical-indicator ML forecasts pay in dollars
Blends Random Forest 60% with Gradient Boosting 40%
Cuts MAE 3% yet loses to a zero-return benchmark on OOS R2
Long-only rule trims drawdown but returns just 2.1% CAGR
en.data: CRSP daily S&P 500, 6,266 days from January 2000 to May 2024; trained 2000-2019, held out 2020-2024.
en.method: Convex ensemble of a 200-tree Random Forest and a 400-stage Gradient Boosting regressor.
en.one_liner: Tree ensembles forecast daily S&P 500 returns but earn almost nothing after costs.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: data is trivially available from free price feeds, but the authors themselves report no tradable edge.
en.takeaway: Use MACD and 21-day volatility as a risk-throttle overlay, not as a standalone alpha signal.

bullets: 기술적 지표 기반 ML 예측이 실제로 돈이 되는지 검증
랜덤포레스트 60%와 그래디언트부스팅 40%를 볼록 결합
MAE는 3% 개선했으나 제로 수익률 벤치마크도 못 이겼다
롱온리 규칙은 낙폭을 줄였지만 연복리 2.1%에 그쳤다
ko.data: CRSP의 S&P 500 일간 데이터 6,266일(2000년 1월~2024년 5월), 2000~2019년 학습에 2020~2024년 홀드아웃 검증이다.
ko.method: 랜덤포레스트(200 트리)와 그래디언트부스팅(400 스테이지)을 6:4로 섞은 앙상블 회귀다.
ko.one_liner: 트리 앙상블로 S&P 500 일간 수익률을 예측했지만 수익은 남지 않았다
ko.relevance_why: CRSP 없이도 무료 가격 데이터로 그대로 재현되지만 저자 스스로 수익성을 부정해 매매 규칙으로는 약해 3점이다.
ko.takeaway: 알파 신호로 쓰기보다 MACD와 21일 변동성을 리스크 축소 필터로 붙이는 정도가 현실적이다.

ssrn-7367199.title: Predictive Analytics for Stock Market Trends Using Ensemble Machine Learning Models

ssrn-7367200.abstract: Stock-level information produced by many active managers can aggregate into a public signal about the overall market. We show that daily return spreads between stocks with high and low active-manager ownership forecast next-day S&P 500 futures and ETF returns; market-timing strategies based on these spreads earn Sharpe ratios near one. Predictability concentrates among hedge funds and highly active mutual funds, strengthens in recessions and high-uncertainty states, exhibits no reversals, persists longer in tight-funding periods, and extends to global markets. A rational-expectations theory of specialized managers and slow-moving capital reconciles these findings and delivers new mechanisms of information aggregation. Structural estimation implies that market-wide information accounts for about 20% of model-implied stock-level signal variation among stocks heavily owned by active managers.

bullets: Asks how stock-level manager research aggregates into a market signal
Builds a daily spread on active-manager ownership rank
Timing strategies on that spread earn Sharpe ratios near one
Hedge funds and highly active mutual funds drive the effect
en.data: Active-manager ownership data with daily S&P 500 futures and ETF returns, extended to global markets; the abstract gives no sample window.
en.method: Sort stocks by active-manager ownership, use the daily long-short spread to forecast the market, and structurally estimate a rational-expectations model of specialized managers and slow-moving capital.
en.one_liner: Return spreads between high and low active-manager-owned stocks predict next-day market returns.
en.relevance_why: The signal is well defined and shows no reversals, but ownership requires stitching quarterly 13F and fund holdings and computing an activeness measure, which is heavy data work.
en.takeaway: Compute the ownership spread daily as a next-day directional input for S&P 500 futures, sized up in recessions and high-uncertainty states.

bullets: 개별 종목 정보가 시장 전체 신호로 뭉치는 경로를 다룬다
보유 비중 상하위 종목의 일별 수익률 격차를 예측 변수로 쓴다
이 격차로 짠 마켓타이밍 전략의 샤프비율이 1 근처다
헤지펀드와 액티브 성향이 강한 뮤추얼펀드에서 예측력이 몰린다
ko.data: 액티브 운용사 보유 비중 자료와 S&P 500 선물·ETF 일별 수익률, 글로벌 시장까지 확장했으나 표본 구간은 초록에 없다
ko.method: 액티브 운용사 보유 비중으로 종목을 나눠 만든 일별 수익률 격차를 예측 변수로 삼고, 전문화된 운용사와 느린 자본 이동을 담은 합리적 기대 모형을 구조 추정했다
ko.one_liner: 액티브 운용사 보유 비중 상하위 종목의 수익률 격차로 다음날 시장을 맞힌다
ko.relevance_why: 신호 정의는 명확하지만 운용사별 보유 비중은 13F와 펀드 보유 명세를 분기 단위로 붙여야 하고 액티브 정도까지 따로 계산해야 해서 데이터 준비 부담이 크다
ko.takeaway: 보유 비중 격차를 일별로 계산해 S&P 500 선물 익일 방향 베팅에 쓰되, 불황과 불확실성이 높은 국면에서 비중을 키운다

ssrn-7367200.title: Between the Bells: Active Management and the Aggregation of Market-Wide Information

ssrn-7367558.abstract: U.S. regulators are adopting large-load tariffs to allocate the financial risk created when utilities build long-lived infrastructure for data centers and other concentrated loads. This paper studies 15 regulator-verified, exact-dated first final tariff decisions covering 13 listed utility parents and 13 states from 2022 through 2026. Customer-specific special-contract approvals are excluded from the primary sample. Expected returns are estimated over trading days [-120,-21]; the primary event window is [-1,+1]. Repeated decisions are collapsed to listed-parent means for exact sign-flip inference. The mean SPY-model cumulative abnormal return is 0.39 percentage points (p = 0.353; bootstrap 95 percent interval:-0.40 to 1.14), providing no evidence of average repricing under the primary model. The XLUadjusted [-1,+1] estimate is positive, but alternative timing windows and influence checks weaken it, making the valuation conclusion benchmark-, window-, and influence-sensitive. A transparent mean-adjusted log-volume measure rises by 0.150 log points, or approximately 16.2 percent. The parent-level result is positive (p = 0.028) but does not survive event-date aggregation (p = 0.110). The log post/pre realized-risk ratio is not distinguishable from zero. The evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, a dependence-sensitive attention response; valuation conclusions are not robust across specifications. The design cannot identify project-level incidence or downstream ratepayer effects.

bullets: Do data-center tariff rulings move utility stocks?
15 dated rulings, [-1,+1] cumulative abnormal return
CAR 0.39pp, p=0.353 — no average repricing
Volume rises 16.2%, but fails event-date aggregation
en.data: 15 regulator-verified first final tariff decisions across 13 states and 13 listed utility parents, 2022 through 2026, with daily returns and volume.
en.method: Estimate expected returns over days [-120,-21] against SPY and XLU, then test [-1,+1] CARs, mean-adjusted log volume, and post/pre realized-risk ratios with sign-flip inference and bootstrap intervals.
en.one_liner: An event study asks whether large-load tariff rulings reprice listed utilities. They mostly don't.
en.relevance_why: The decision dates must be hand-collected from state regulators and the sample is only 15 events, so there is no rule a machine can trade.
en.takeaway: Treat tariff decision dates as a volume-spike risk flag on utility names, not as a directional signal.

bullets: 데이터센터 전력 요금제 결정이 주가에 반영되나
15건 규제 결정, [-1,+1] 누적초과수익 측정
CAR 0.39%p, p=0.353으로 재평가 근거 없음
거래량은 16.2% 늘지만 날짜 집계 시 유의성 소멸
ko.data: 2022~2026년 미국 13개 주, 상장 유틸리티 모회사 13곳에 걸친 규제기관 확인 최초 최종 요금제 결정 15건과 해당 종목의 일별 수익률·거래량이다.
ko.method: SPY와 XLU를 벤치마크로 삼아 [-120,-21] 구간에서 기대수익을 추정한 뒤 [-1,+1] 누적초과수익(CAR)과 평균조정 로그 거래량, 사후/사전 실현위험 비율을 부호 반전 검정과 부트스트랩으로 따진다.
ko.one_liner: 대형 부하 요금제 승인이 유틸리티 주가를 움직이는지 이벤트 스터디로 검증했다
ko.relevance_why: 규제 결정의 정확한 날짜를 직접 손으로 모아야 하고 표본이 15건뿐이라 자동 매매 규칙으로 옮기기 어렵다
ko.takeaway: 요금제 결정일 전후로 유틸리티 종목의 거래량 급증을 예상할 수는 있으나 방향성 베팅 근거는 없으니 이벤트 회피용 리스크 필터로만 쓴다

ssrn-7367558.title: Large-Load Tariff Decisions and Utility Market Responses

ssrn-7367700.abstract: This paper examines the valuation, token economics, market structure, and risk profile of HYPE, the native token of Hyperliquid, an on-chain derivatives and financial infrastructure platform. The analysis focuses on the economic relationship between Hyperliquid's protocol activity and HYPE through the Assistance Fund's open-market acquisition and permanent burn mechanism, while separating token utility from legal equity ownership. It evaluates HYPE using multiple annualized protocol-revenue methodologies, revenue-multiple frameworks, supply and dilution analysis, and a scenario-based valuation framework. The paper also examines the August 2026 repricing through regulatory catalysts, derivatives positioning, liquidity, and market structure, and assesses Hyperliquid's competitive position, regulatory exposure, ecosystem expansion, and reflexivity risks. The analysis finds that HYPE possesses an unusually direct and measurable value-capture mechanism, but that the token's valuation already embeds substantial expectations for revenue durability, market-share retention, ecosystem diversification, and continued supply absorption. The paper concludes with explicit conditions under which the investment thesis would strengthen or fail.

bullets: Asks whether HYPE's price is justified by protocol revenue
Uses revenue multiples, dilution and scenario valuation
Value capture is direct, but expectations are already priced
en.data: Hyperliquid protocol revenue and token supply figures, with a focused look at the August 2026 repricing.
en.method: Annualized protocol-revenue estimates, revenue-multiple comparisons, supply and dilution analysis, and scenario valuation.
en.one_liner: Valuation study of HYPE, the Hyperliquid protocol token.
en.relevance_why: On-chain revenue data is public and easy to pull, but this is single-token fundamental analysis with no entry or exit rules to automate.
en.takeaway: Use the author's stated thesis-break conditions as a checklist before sizing or cutting a HYPE position.

bullets: 토큰 가격이 프로토콜 수익에 값하는지 따진다
연환산 수익, 수익 배수, 희석, 시나리오로 평가
가치 포착 경로는 뚜렷하나 기대가 이미 가격에 반영
ko.data: 하이퍼리퀴드 프로토콜 수익과 토큰 공급 데이터를 쓰고 2026년 8월 재평가 구간을 따로 살핀다.
ko.method: 연환산 프로토콜 수익 추정, 수익 배수 비교, 공급·희석 분석, 시나리오별 밸류에이션을 섞어 쓴다.

ko.takeaway: HYPE 롱을 잡을지 접을지 판단할 때 저자가 정리한 논지 붕괴 조건을 체크리스트로 쓴다.

ssrn-7367700.title: HYPE: The $18 Billion Question — Can Hyperliquid Outgrow its Valuation?

ssrn-7368018.abstract: Bitcoin maximalists, individuals who invest exclusively in Bitcoin and reject diversification across other cryptocurrencies, theoretically constitute a significant segment within the broader crypto investor population. This paper investigates whether these investors really differ systematically from other cryptocurrency investors in terms of financial attitudes, and socio-demographic characteristics. Using microdata from the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Payment Choice (SCPC), the analysis shows that maximalists are more likely to be older-each additional year of age increases the probability of being a maximalist by about 0.3-0.4 percentage points, male, and have lower household income-being in a higher income category reduces this likelihood by roughly 1 percentage point, a profile consistent with early adoption and a stronger attachment to Bitcoin. In addition, those motivated by speculation or who have sold cryptocurrency in the past year are 11-16 percentage points less likely to be maximalists, indicating a preference for long-term holding over opportunistic trading.
ssrn-7368018.affiliations: Comillas Pontifical University - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Faculty of Economics and Management of Sfax. and Comillas Pontifical University - Department of Financial Management

bullets: Nobody had checked if maximalists are a real segment
Regressions on Federal Reserve SCPC microdata
Each year of age raises maximalist odds 0.3-0.4pp
Speculators and recent sellers: 11-16pp less likely
en.data: Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Payment Choice microdata; the abstract names no survey years.
en.method: Discrete-choice regressions on survey microdata, reported as marginal effects.
en.one_liner: Survey data tests whether Bitcoin-only investors differ from other crypto holders.
en.relevance_why: Scores 1 because it is an investor-profile survey with no entry or exit rules, and SCPC microdata is not a feed you can wire into a backtest.
en.takeaway: Background color on who holds Bitcoin through drawdowns, not a signal you can code.

bullets: 비트코인 단일 투자자가 정말 별개 집단인지 미확인
연준 SCPC 설문 마이크로데이터로 회귀 분석

ko.method: 연준 소비자 결제선택 설문 마이크로데이터에 이산선택 회귀를 돌려 한계효과를 뽑았다.
ko.one_liner: 비트코인만 사는 투자자가 다른 코인 투자자와 어떻게 다른지 설문으로 따졌다.
ko.relevance_why: 설문 기반 투자자 프로필 연구라 진입·청산 규칙이 없고 SCPC 마이크로데이터는 가격 데이터처럼 바로 붙일 수 없어 1점이다.
ko.takeaway: 매매 규칙으로 옮길 건 없고 비트코인 보유층의 매도 성향을 가늠하는 배경 지식 정도다.

ssrn-7368018.title: All in on Bitcoin: Are Maximalists Really Different?

ssrn-7369139.abstract: Predictive models are often validated against post-deployment outcomes even when modelguided decisions help produce them. In a multi-lender refinancing model, greater assessment commonality turns diversified false rejections into joint rejection. Induced defaults then raise measured accuracy while unanimous negative assessments become less informative about borrower fundamentals. More accurate but more common technologies can therefore improve validation while increasing refinancing fragility. Controlled model-diversity exercises and lender-state evidence support the covariance and rescue mechanisms. The result extends beyond credit to consequential prediction systems in which multiple decision makers use correlated technologies and jointly affect the outcomes used for validation.
ssrn-7369139.affiliations: RWTH Aachen University - Department of Finance

bullets: Models get validated on outcomes the models themselves caused
Multi-lender refinancing model, varying assessment commonality
Correlated errors become joint rejection, which induces defaults

ssrn-7369221.abstract: Digital attention is widely used as an input in financial models, but different data sources may lead to different conclusions. We test whether financial findings remain stable when the attention proxy is replaced while the sample, timing, outcomes, estimator, and inferential framework are held constant. Using Google Trends, Wikipedia pageviews, GDELT news intensity, and consensus measures for 57 US firms from 2016 to 2025, we examine trading volume, forward volatility, contemporaneous and forward returns, attention around earnings announcements, and out-of-sample forecasting. Volume and earnings-event conclusions remain stable across sources. Forward-volatility effects are consistently positive but differ in inferential strength, whereas return effects are small, sign-unstable, and provide no out-of-sample forecasting gains. These results show that strong empirical relationships are robust to reasonable measurement choices, while weaker findings are more source-dependent. We therefore treat data-source selection as a component of model uncertainty and propose controlled proxy substitution as a diagnostic for inferential fragility in intelligent financial systems.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

en.relevance_why: Google Trends, Wikipedia and GDELT are all free, but this delivers a diagnostic procedure, not entry and exit rules.
en.takeaway: Use controlled proxy substitution as a robustness gate before trading any attention-based signal.

ssrn-7369279.abstract: Decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePINs) are increasingly presented as investable exposure to the computing, connectivity, and energy infrastructure underpinning articial intelligence. We examine whether this narrative is reected in market prices or whether DePIN tokens behave primarily as crypto-risk assets. Using 1,065 common trading days from May 2022 to August 2026, we analyze functionally selected DePIN tokens alongside semiconductors, utilities, uranium, natural gas, Bitcoin, and Ether. The empirical design combines dynamic connectedness with xed-dimension factor ltering to distinguish infrastructure-related transmission from common crypto-market exposure, followed by out-of-sample portfolio tests of its economic relevance. Bitcoin and Ether dominate shock transmission. Filtering common crypto exposure reduces connectedness among the thematic assets from 36.3% to 20.0%, while broader market controls lower it to 17.8%, leaving only a modest residual DePIN-infrastructure channel. This linkage is strongly state dependent, increasing approximately vefold in both market tails relative to the median, and 90.95% of its absolute magnitude is concentrated within one to ve trading days. A stricter compute-only specication restricted to Render Network (RENDER) and Akash Network (AKT) produces the same economic classication. Moreover, adding DePIN tokens to physical-infrastructure portfolios generates no robust out-of-sample improvement in risk-adjusted performance. The results show that protocol function does not automatically translate into nancial exposure to the underlying infrastructure: the studied DePIN tokens behave predominantly as cryptorisk assets with a modest, state-dependent, and transient infrastructure component.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

en.takeaway: Stop treating DePIN as an infrastructure substitute; hedge crypto beta first, then trade the residual link only as a 1-5 day tail signal.

ssrn-7369458.abstract: This paper separates two claims conflated in the style-investing literature: that a firm's growth/value direction predicts risk, and that its extremity-distance from the ambiguous midpoint-predicts risk incrementally to direction. In a survivorship-free, point-in-time panel of 6,546 U.S. common stocks (market cap ≥ $300 million, 2004-2025, 196,438 firm-quarters), we run a horse race between the signed rank and its own extremity transform on three independent constructions. On price-to-sales, extremity is the whole story: direction is null (t =-0.25) while extremity survives fully intact (t = 9.7)-a genuine, if economically modest (0.050 SD), effect and our cleanest identification. On price, both terms survive jointly (direction t =-4.2, extremity t = 14.2), reported only as an upper bound given disclosed mechanical volatility content. On book-to-market the pattern inverts entirely: extremity collapses to zero (t = 0.43) once direction is included, while direction stays large (t = 17.2)-what looked like extremity is the familiar growth-options finding that low-book-to-market firms are more volatile (Cao, Simin, and Zhao 2008), not a distance-from-median effect. A battery of six placebo extremity transforms from characteristics unrelated to valuation (size, beta, bookto-market, momentum, MAX, idiosyncratic skewness) shows this symmetric pattern is not unique to valuation-all six predict forward idiosyncratic volatility, two more strongly than price-to-sales extremity itself-yet price-to-sales extremity survives every pairwise and joint test against them (t = 8.2 jointly, a 15% attenuation from its solo t = 9.9): a genuine incremental fact, not a newly documented class of risk determinant. Economic value concentrates in the price-based measure, which improves out-of-sample volatility forecasts against HAR-RV and EGARCH benchmarks (Clark-West t ≥ 3.4) and lowers realized portfolio volatility in 18 of 18 sample years, surviving a correlation-matched synthetic placebo. The identifying price-to-sales measure adds far less out-of-sample value and no portfolio benefit, and there is no return premium to either (t = 0.7): style extremity is a risk characteristic, not a return anomaly.
