ssrn-7379779.abstract: We estimate a two-state Gaussian-mixture hidden Markov model for daily Brent crude, gold, silver, and natural gas futures in which transition probabilities depend on lagged geopolitical risk (GPR). Using the threat and act components of the daily GPR index, we find that realised geopolitical acts are associated with greater stress-regime persistence: a one-standard-deviation increase in act elevation is associated with roughly 45 to 51 percent higher odds of remaining stressed. Threat effects are concentrated on entry from calm but are weaker and not robust to the full control set. Nested likelihoodratio tests reject dropping the geopolitical block from the transition kernel. The results indicate that the geopolitical association is strongest through regime duration rather than through a simple level effect on volatility.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Tests whether GPR shifts volatility level or regime duration
Two-state Gaussian HMM with GPR-driven transition probabilities
One-SD act shock raises stay-stressed odds 45-51 percent
Threat effects hit entry only, fade under full controls
en.data: Daily Brent, gold, silver, and natural gas futures plus the daily GPR index; the abstract gives no sample window.
en.method: Two-state Gaussian-mixture HMM whose transition kernel is a function of lagged GPR threat and act components.
en.one_liner: Geopolitical acts, not threats, keep commodity markets stuck in stress regimes.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: the daily GPR index and futures prices are free and public, but the paper gives no entry or exit rules, so the strategy layer is yours to build.
en.takeaway: Use the GPR act component to extend expected stress-regime duration, then cut leverage and widen stops on commodity books.

ko.method: 전이확률을 시차 지정학위험(GPR)의 위협·사건 성분에 연동한 2국면 가우시안 혼합 은닉마코프 모형(HMM)을 쓴다.

ko.takeaway: GPR 사건 성분이 튀면 원자재 포지션의 스트레스 국면 예상 지속일을 늘려 잡고 레버리지와 손절 폭을 미리 조정한다.

ssrn-7379989.abstract: The relevant empirical question about momentum in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) is not whether it works, but whether simple operational rules can extract value from it. We show that pure momentum over a broad ETF universe creates no value: replicated across 3,215 investable U.S. ETFs, it delivers Sharpe ratios between −0.17 and +0.22 with drawdowns of 69% to 82%, systematically below passive investing. Yet three layers of rules available to any investor fully reverse that conclusion. We evaluate the 2001–2026 period (1,289 weeks) across the investable universe, charging a 20-basis-point transaction cost per side at every stage of the analysis. On top of replicating classic cross-sectional momentum, we add technical entry signals, a multi-horizon momentum ranking with mandatory diversification across super-categories within an eight-position portfolio, and an expanded family of 144 dynamic stop-loss and take-profit exit rules, all under an asymmetric rebalancing regime of biweekly purchases and weekly exit monitoring. The complete strategy delivers a Sharpe ratio above 1.3 and a maximum drawdown of −7%, beating passive investing by close to a full Sharpe point; the alpha concentrates in tail-risk reduction and is impaired only during the high-implied-volatility regime. The central implication for researchers and practitioners is that the value comes not from the technical signal but from the operational management layer that surrounds it.
ssrn-7379989.affiliations: Universidad Diego Portales and Universidad Diego Portales

bullets: Pure ETF momentum loses to passive, so what fixes it?
Add technical entries, multi-horizon ranks, 144 exit rules
Sharpe rises above 1.3; max drawdown shrinks to -7%
Alpha comes from tail-risk cuts, not the signal
en.data: 3,215 investable U.S. ETFs over 2001-2026, 1,289 weeks, charging 20 bps per side at every stage.
en.method: Classic cross-sectional momentum plus technical entry filters, an eight-position multi-horizon rank with forced super-category diversification, and 144 dynamic stop-loss/take-profit exits under biweekly buys and weekly exit checks.
en.one_liner: ETF momentum pays only when operational rules wrap it.
en.relevance_why: Rules, universe and cadence are fully specified on public ETF prices, and it also refutes plain ETF momentum, whose Sharpe runs -0.17 to +0.22 with 69-82% drawdowns.
en.takeaway: Bolt the exit-rule and diversification layer onto an existing momentum sleeve to cut drawdowns.

ssrn-7379989.title: Momentum Strategies in ETFs under Simple Operational Rules: Economic Value and Conditional Predictability

ssrn-7379990.abstract: The information investors acquire in financial markets has various forms. We refer to range information as information about the upper and lower bound which the payoff of an asset may reach in the future. This study develops rational expectation models to explore the market impacts of investors' asymmetrical acquisition of range information. Uninformed traders are inherently unable to directly obtain the private signal held by informed traders. Our model shows that when range information is released to investors asymmetrically, uninformed traders who can only obtain rougher range information will not trade assets under the max-min ambiguity aversion criterion. Investors' asymmetrical acquisition of range information can cause that market liquidity and the sensitivity of market price to private signal vary continuously with the signal and noise trading volume. Our model also reveals that investors' asymmetrical acquisition of range information can decrease market liquidity and increase the sensitivity of price under some conditions and we also specify these conditions.
ssrn-7379990.affiliations: Shandong Normal University, Shandong University of Finance and Economics and Shandong University of Finance and Economics

bullets: Prior asymmetry models focus on signal precision, not bounds
Defines range information: the payoff's upper and lower limits
Solves a rational expectations equilibrium with ambiguity aversion
Traders holding only coarse bounds stop trading entirely
en.data: Theory only
en.method: A rational expectations equilibrium where uninformed traders optimize under a max-min ambiguity aversion criterion.
en.one_liner: Models how asymmetric access to an asset's payoff bounds reshapes liquidity and price sensitivity.
en.relevance_why: Pure theory with zero trading rules, and the model's range information has no observable counterpart in market data.
en.takeaway: A lens for reading why spreads widen in names with severe information asymmetry — no signal to trade.

ssrn-7380038.abstract: Providing liquidity on decentralized exchanges earns fees but exposes liquidity providers (LPs) to impermanent loss from price movements. With concentrated liquidity, LPs control this risk by choosing how narrowly to deploy capital around the price. Using option prices, we quantify the cost of liquidity provision by developing measures of implied impermanent loss for concentrated liquidity and define the associated impermanent loss risk premium. Empirically, higher expected impermanent loss widens liquidity ranges, while higher risk premia re-center and tighten liquidity around the spot price, highlighting opposing effects of risk and compensation.
ssrn-7380038.affiliations: , North Carolina State University - Department of Mathematics and University of Turin - Collegio Carlo Alberto

bullets: No market-based price existed for the LP's loss exposure
Options imply expected impermanent loss and its risk premium
Higher expected loss widens ranges; higher premia tighten them
Risk and compensation push range choice in opposite directions
en.data: Crypto option prices plus concentrated-liquidity pool range data; the abstract states no evaluation window.
en.method: Extract risk-neutral distributions from option prices, map them to concentrated-liquidity payoffs, and define the premium as the gap to realized loss.
en.one_liner: Prices impermanent loss for concentrated liquidity from option prices.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: the range-sizing logic is codeable, but there are no entry/exit rules and you must join crypto option chains with on-chain pool data yourself.
en.takeaway: Feed option-implied impermanent loss into how wide and where you center an LP range.

ko.relevance_why: 구간 폭과 중심을 정하는 규칙으로 옮길 여지는 있지만 진입·청산 규칙이 없고 암호자산 옵션 체인과 온체인 풀 데이터를 함께 붙여야 해서 3점이다

ssrn-7380038.title: Implied Impermanent Loss for Concentrated Liquidity

ssrn-7380538.abstract: Emerging-market joint ventures (JVs) frequently rely on foreign technology to navigate institutional voids-regulatory ambiguity, fragmented supply chains, and infrastructure deficits-yet many struggle to convert this knowledge into global export capability. Prior research typically models foreign technology licencing, internal R&D, and external search as discrete, additive inputs; we instead conceptualise them as an interdependent configuration. We ask how JVs recombine these heterogeneous knowledge sources to build export capability under resource scarcity. Using an abductive, longitudinal process-tracing design across ten legal entities in eight Indian manufacturing and life-science contexts (FY2015-FY2025), we prioritise audited statutory and regulatory disclosures to mitigate self-reporting bias. We find that successful JVs follow a sequential process-then-product pathway whose ordering is dictated by resource scarcity. We refine absorptive capacity theory by showing that realised absorptive capacity functions as a threshold condition rather than a continuous, linear moderator. Below this critical capability floor, foreign licencing deepens technological dependence; above it, JVs configure inbound open innovation as an active institutional buffer, transforming domestic compliance constraints into scalable export capabilities. Export readiness thus depends less on the raw volume of innovation inputs than on the architectural alignment of local R&D and technical governance.

bullets: Rejects treating licensing, R&D and external search as additive inputs
Process-traces 10 legal entities across 8 Indian sites, FY2015-FY2025
Absorptive capacity acts as a threshold, not a linear moderator
Below the floor, licensing deepens dependence; above it, exports scale
en.data: Audited statutory and regulatory disclosures, FY2015 through FY2025.
en.method: Abductive longitudinal process tracing across ten matched case entities.
en.one_liner: Traces ten Indian JVs to find when licensed foreign tech becomes export capability.
en.relevance_why: Scored 1: a case study with no prices, signals or cross-section, and the audited filings must be hand-read entity by entity.
en.takeaway: Nothing to code; at best a qualitative screen for Indian small-cap manufacturers pairing licensing deals with in-house R&D spend.

bullets: 기술도입·자체 R&D·외부탐색을 따로 더하는 기존 모형을 문제 삼는다
인도 제조·생명과학 8개 현장 10개 법인을 10년간 과정추적했다
흡수역량이 문턱값으로 작동한다. 문턱 아래면 기술종속만 깊어진다
문턱을 넘은 합작사는 공정 먼저, 제품 나중 순서로 수출력을 쌓았다
ko.data: 감사받은 법정·규제 공시 자료, FY2015~FY2025 10년 구간이다.
ko.method: 귀추적 종단 과정추적(process tracing)으로 10개 법인의 사례를 비교했다.
ko.one_liner: 인도 합작사 10곳을 추적해 기술도입이 수출력으로 바뀌는 조건을 밝혔다.
ko.relevance_why: 가격도 신호도 없는 사례 연구라 자동화할 대상이 없고, 감사 공시를 법인별로 손으로 읽어야 해서 데이터 구축 비용도 크다.
ko.takeaway: 매매 규칙으로 옮길 거리가 없다. 인도 중소형 제조주를 볼 때 기술도입 계약과 자체 R&D 지출을 같이 확인하라는 정성 체크리스트 정도다.

ssrn-7380538.title: From Institutional Constraints to Global Reach: Open Innovation and Export Capability in Emerging-market Joint Ventures

ssrn-7381318.abstract: Foreign-exchange intervention is usually judged by the direction of the exchange-rate movement, yet an operation can move the yen without reducing the risk surrounding that path. This paper studies the timing of USD/JPY volatility around 69 Japanese intervention episodes between May 1991 and July 2024. Daily variance is measured against each episode's own 20-trading-day pre-event benchmark, and the intervention day is separated from the following 5-, 10-, and 20-day windows. Pooled daily variance is 4.2% higher on the intervention day, 19.0% lower over days 1-5, 11.8% lower over days 1-10, and 0.1% lower over days 1-20. No level estimate survives the frozen four-test Holm family, and the three post-event-minus-event-day transfer contrasts are all negative with adjusted pvalues of 1.000, so the data do not support the intuition that intervention buys calm and repays it later. The 20-day outcome is statistically equivalent to its pre-event benchmark inside a pre-specified ±0.20 log-variance region. The pooled path nevertheless conceals a historical contrast: the four 2022-2024 episodes show variance ratios 3.45 and 2.97 times those of the earlier episodes at 5 and 20 days, with exact permutation p-values of 0.033 and 0.006 after Holm adjustment. That contrast rests on four yen-purchase episodes, weakens under controls and leave-one-out checks, and is not reproduced by a locked 2026 holdout whose variance falls 16.7% and 47.4% below baseline at 10 and 20 days. Yield-curve alignment does not explain the volatility path, and intervention size predicts only the contemporaneous response before family adjustment. Because intervention dates are endogenous to market stress, every estimate is an event-time association rather than a causal effect. The evidence rejects a general delayed-risktransfer account and points instead to historically concentrated, nonpersistent volatility consequences.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Tests the belief that intervention defers risk, not removes it
Event study vs each episode's own 20-day pre-window
No level estimate survives the Holm four-test family
en.data: Daily USD/JPY around 69 Japanese intervention episodes, May 1991 to July 2024, plus a locked 2026 holdout.
en.method: Log-variance ratios per window, pooled under a frozen Holm family, with exact permutation tests and a pre-specified ±0.20 equivalence band.
en.one_liner: Tracks USD/JPY volatility around 69 Japanese FX interventions, 1991-2024.
en.relevance_why: USD/JPY prices and MOF intervention dates are free and public, but the paper yields event-time associations rather than entry and exit rules, so it caps at 2.
en.takeaway: Kill any rule that sells vol into a yen intervention expecting a later payback, and treat the 2022-2024 yen-purchase regime as its own sample.

bullets: 개입이 변동성을 뒤로 미룬다는 통념을 검증했다
직전 20일 분산을 기준선으로 삼은 이벤트 분석이다
Holm 보정 후 살아남는 수준 추정치가 없다
ko.data: 1991년 5월부터 2024년 7월까지 일본 개입 69건의 USD/JPY 일별 데이터, 2026년 홀드아웃을 따로 잠가뒀다.
ko.method: 구간별 로그분산비를 Holm 4검정군으로 묶고 정확 순열검정과 ±0.20 동등성 구간을 함께 썼다.
ko.one_liner: 일본 외환개입 69건 뒤 엔화 변동성이 어떻게 움직였는지 따졌다
ko.relevance_why: USD/JPY 가격과 재무성 개입 공시는 누구나 받을 수 있지만 매매 룰이 아니라 사후 연관성만 남아서 2점이다.
ko.takeaway: 엔 개입일에 변동성 매도 포지션을 깔아두는 식의 룰은 근거가 없으니 접고, 2022~2024년처럼 개입 성격이 바뀐 구간만 따로 다루는 게 낫다.

ssrn-7381658.abstract: The third derivative of bond price with respect to yield, the analogue of gamma for fixed income, has been derived before but treated as a deterministic curiosity of marginal importance. This paper advances and tests a single hypothesis: that this third-order term is economically material during macroeconomic crises, with a contribution to expected price change governed jointly by maturity, the size of the yield move, and the asymmetry of the yield-change distribution. We treat the yield change as a random variable and establish a two-stage existence theorem. Under a normal distribution with non-zero drift the term acts through a puredrift channel and a drift-variance channel; the Normal-Inverse Gaussian extension adds exactly one further term, a pure-skewness channel proportional to the third cumulant that vanishes under any symmetric distribution. Empirically, across the 1973-74 oil shock, the 2000-02 dot-com deflation, the 2007-09 global financial crisis, and the COVID-19 2020 shock measured with Adrian-Crump-Moench data, the third-order sensitivity scales cubically with maturity (a thirty-year to two-year ratio of roughly 525 to 690 across the three historical crises, and about 1380 in the low-yield COVID window), the gamma-to-convexity ratio rises from 1.9 percent at two years to 17.5 percent at thirty years at crisis-scale moves and holds at a stable 0.76 of the Brooks-Livingston convexity-to-duration ratio, and the skewness channel reaches 48 to 86 percent of the drift channels for thirty-year bonds, offsetting most of the normal-distribution gamma contribution in the dot-com episode. The skewness condition itself is confirmed decisively in daily settlement data for five CME Treasury futures contracts, with a pooled statistic of χ²(3) = 73.4 and significant within-window skewness in the dot-com episode, while the global financial crisis window is fattailed rather than skewed; the shorter monthly windows lack the power to reject symmetry on their own. The third-order term is negligible in the small, symmetric setting examined by earlier work and material in the large, directional, asymmetric moves that characterize crises.

bullets: Prior work dismissed the third-order term as a deterministic curiosity
Treats yield change as random, proves a two-stage existence theorem
Gamma-to-convexity climbs from 1.9% at 2y to 17.5% at 30y
en.data: Adrian-Crump-Moench yields across the 1973-74 oil shock, 2000-02 dot-com, 2007-09 GFC and 2020 COVID windows, with skewness tested on daily settlements for five CME Treasury futures (pooled χ²(3) = 73.4).
en.method: Decomposes the third-order term into pure-drift and drift-variance channels under a normal yield distribution, plus one pure-skewness channel under a Normal-Inverse Gaussian.
en.one_liner: The third derivative of bond price to yield matters in crises, not in calm markets.
en.relevance_why: ACM curves and CME settlements are free and public, so replication is cheap, but this is a risk-pricing correction rather than an entry/exit rule, so it needs real strategy design on top.
en.takeaway: Add the third-order term to P&L approximations for long-maturity crisis positions and tilt duration hedges by the sign of yield skewness.

bullets: 3차 항은 그동안 무시해도 되는 상수 취급을 받았다
수익률 변화를 확률변수로 놓고 2단계 존재정리를 세웠다
30년물에서 감마/컨벡시티 비율이 17.5%까지 올라간다
ko.data: Adrian-Crump-Moench 수익률 곡선으로 1973-74 오일쇼크, 2000-02 닷컴 붕괴, 2007-09 금융위기, 2020 코로나 국면을 다뤘고 CME 국채선물 5종 일별 정산가로 왜도를 검정했다
ko.method: 수익률 변화에 정규분포와 정규-역가우시안(Normal-Inverse Gaussian)을 각각 적용해 순수 드리프트, 드리프트-분산, 순수 왜도 세 채널로 3차 항을 분해한다
ko.one_liner: 채권 가격의 3차 미분항이 위기 국면에서 실제로 돈이 된다는 걸 검증했다
ko.relevance_why: ACM 곡선과 CME 선물 정산가 모두 공개 데이터라 재현은 쉽지만 매수·매도 규칙이 아니라 리스크 계산식이라 전략으로 만들려면 설계가 더 필요해 3점이다
ko.takeaway: 위기 국면 장기물 포지션의 손익 근사에 3차 항을 넣고 왜도 부호에 따라 듀레이션 헤지 비율을 조정한다

ssrn-7381810.abstract: Most machine learning trading strategies are judged by their annualized return, that is, the average gain or loss over a year. That figure says nothing about the speed of the price movements that produce it. We take a machine learning portfolio built for Bursa Malaysia, rebuild its daily returns exactly from its stored holdings over 2022 to 2025, and split those returns into layers by how long each movement lasts, from two-day fluctuations to trends beyond 128 trading days. We then compare every layer with five Malaysian benchmark indices and four global market forces. The results show two distinct parts. At horizons beyond six months, it simply rides the Malaysian market. At the one-quarter to half-year horizon it moves almost independently of the large-cap index, with a beta of 0.09, and this independent layer is unchanged after trading costs. Its co-movement with the market is confined to crisis episodes, and no global force tracks it.
ssrn-7381810.affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN
authors: Ahmad Shauqi bin Haji Mohamad Zubir
Wan Nurul Nisrin binti Wan Mohd Zamani

bullets: Annualized return hides which horizon actually earns the money
Rebuilds daily returns from holdings, layers them 2 to 128+ days
Beyond six months the strategy just rides the Malaysian market
Quarter-to-half-year layer: beta 0.09, survives trading costs
en.data: One Bursa Malaysia ML portfolio's holdings, 2022-2025, plus 5 Malaysian benchmark indices and 4 global market factors.
en.method: Rebuild daily returns from stored holdings, decompose into duration layers, regress each layer on 5 Malaysian indices and 4 global forces.
en.one_liner: Splits an ML portfolio's returns by movement duration to locate its alpha.
en.relevance_why: A post-hoc attribution method, not a trading rule, and the specific ML portfolio's holdings are proprietary to the authors, though the technique applies to any strategy whose daily returns you own.
en.takeaway: Use it as a diagnostic: split your own strategy's returns by horizon to separate beta-riding layers from genuinely independent ones.

bullets: 연율 수익률만으로는 알파가 어느 속도에서 나오는지 모른다
일별 수익을 2일~128일 이상 시간 층으로 분해했다
6개월 초과 구간은 그냥 시장 추종이었다
분기~반기 층은 대형주 지수 베타 0.09로 거의 독립이다
ko.data: 2022~2025년 부르사 말레이시아 ML 포트폴리오의 보유 기록과 말레이시아 지수 5개, 글로벌 시장 요인 4개
ko.method: 저장된 보유 종목에서 일별 수익을 복원한 뒤 지속 기간별 층으로 나누고 층마다 벤치마크 5개와 글로벌 요인 4개에 회귀했다
ko.one_liner: ML 포트폴리오 수익을 보유 기간별로 쪼개 알파의 출처를 찾았다
ko.relevance_why: 매매 규칙이 아니라 사후 분해 기법이라 전략화하려면 설계가 더 필요하고, 대상 ML 포트폴리오의 보유 기록은 저자 고유 자산이라 외부에서 못 구한다
ko.takeaway: 기존 전략 수익을 기간별로 쪼개 시장 추종 층과 진짜 독립 층을 갈라내는 성과 진단 도구로 쓴다

ssrn-7381919.abstract: Quantum illumination has been proposed as a theoretical route to detecting low-reflectivity targets, such as stealth aircraft, in high-background-noise environments where classical radar performance degrades. The protocol, as originally formulated (Lloyd, 2008; Tan et al., 2008), uses continuous-variable entangled light (two-mode squeezed vacuum) and a specific phase-sensitive joint receiver to achieve a theoretical detection advantage over classical illumination of matched energy, even though the entanglement itself does not survive the round trip through a lossy, noisy channel. This study investigates whether that advantage appears in a simpler, discrete-variable (qubit) toy model, of the kind commonly used for pedagogical intuition, implemented on PKTron and cross-checked on IBM Quantum hardware. A rigorously fair comparison was constructed in which an entangled Bell pair and a classically correlated (separable) mixture of matched initial correlation strength were each subjected to identical loss and background-noise channels, with detection performance assessed via the same joint correlation measurement (Z⊗ Z expectation) in both cases. In PKTron simulation, the entangled probe showed a correlation separation between target-present and target-absent hypotheses of 0.0100 at zero background noise, decreasing to 0.0025 at high background noise, while the classically correlated probe showed a substantially larger separation, decreasing from 0.1000 to 0.0500 over the same range-indicating no entanglement advantage, and if anything, a disadvantage, in this discrete model. This qualitative finding was independently corroborated on IBM Quantum's ibm_kingston hardware, using natural qubit T1 relaxation (rather than an artificially injected noise parameter) as the loss channel: entangled correlation degraded to 54.5% of its initial value after 60 microseconds, compared to 77.7% retained by the classically correlated mixture over the same interval. These results indicate that the theoretical quantum illumination advantage does not straightforwardly emerge from a simple discrete-qubit correlation model, consistent with the broader understanding that the effect is specific to continuousvariable Gaussian states and phase-sensitive joint detection, and consistent with quantum illumination's status as a theoretical concept with no demonstrated range or signal-to-noise advantage over classical radar to date.
ssrn-7381919.affiliations: Centre of Excellence for Technology Quantum and AI Canada
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Tests whether the CV entanglement edge survives in qubit models
Bell pair vs. separable mixture, same loss and noise channels
Entangled separation 0.0100 vs. classical 0.1000 — ten times worse
IBM ibm_kingston: 54.5% vs. 77.7% correlation retained at 60μs
en.data: Theory only — PKTron simulation plus IBM ibm_kingston hardware runs, no financial data.
en.method: Matched-correlation Bell pair and classically correlated mixture pass identical loss channels, read out by Z⊗Z joint correlation.

en.takeaway: Nothing tradable; useful only as a sanity check on quantum-computing narratives in stock pitches.

벨 쌍과 고전 상관 혼합을 같은 손실·잡음 채널에 통과

ko.method: 벨 쌍과 분리 가능 혼합 상태를 동일한 손실·배경잡음 채널에 넣고 Z⊗Z 결합 상관을 측정했다

ko.takeaway: 트레이딩에 쓸 규칙은 없다. 양자 컴퓨팅 관련 종목의 기술 서사를 검증할 때 참고 자료 정도다

ssrn-7382219.abstract: The United States has increasingly leveraged the Entity List as a key instrument within its export control regime. While existing studies primarily examine the political motivations and macroeconomic consequences of these measures, we extend the literature by empirically investigating the link between U.S. Entity List targeting Chinese entities and stock price crash risk of affected Chinese firms. Utilizing a panel dataset of Chinese listed companies spanning 2012–2023, we find a positive association between U.S. Entity List sanctions and stock price crash risk. The identified channels include increased overseas supply vulnerability, weakened inventory turnover efficiency, and increased managerial risk narrative suppression. U.S. Entity List sanctions particularly increase stock price crash risk in firms with greater internal control deficiencies, lower analyst coverage, more negative investor sentiment, and longer financial disclosure delays. These findings identify targeted export control policy shocks as a novel driver of stock price crash risk, underscoring the need for policymakers to anchor market expectations and for listed firms to develop sanction-resilient governance and risk management that foster the sustainable development of financial markets.
ssrn-7382219.affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan University and Sichuan University

bullets: Sanctions research covers politics and macro, not firm crash risk
Panel regressions on Chinese listed firms, 2012-2023
Listed firms show higher stock price crash risk
Effect concentrates in weak internal controls, thin analyst coverage
en.data: Panel of Chinese listed companies, 2012-2023.
en.method: Panel regressions link Entity List designation to crash risk, with overseas supply vulnerability, inventory turnover, and suppressed managerial risk narratives as channels.

en.relevance_why: Score 1: a policy-shock regression with no trading rule; the BIS list is public, but mapping entities to listed tickers and building internal-control and sentiment proxies is heavy manual work.
en.takeaway: Use designation dates as an event-driven risk filter to cut tail exposure on individual China A-share names.

내부통제 부실, 낮은 애널리스트 커버리지에서 효과가 세다

ko.method: 중국 상장사 패널 회귀로 제재 등재와 주가 급락 위험을 연결하고 공급망·재고회전·경영진 위험 서술 억제를 경로로 검증한다
ko.one_liner: 미국 제재 명단 등재가 중국 상장사 주가 급락 위험을 높인다
ko.relevance_why: 정책 충격의 사후 회귀 분석이라 매매 규칙이 없고 BIS 명단 자체는 공개지만 중국 상장사 대응, 내부통제 지표, 투자자 심리 대리변수를 붙이는 데 손이 많이 간다

ssrn-7382221.abstract: Institutional site visits enable investors to obtain incremental information beyond routine public disclosures and engage directly with corporate managers. This study posits that site visits may facilitate the early transmission of event-related information to the market, thereby contributing to price reactions before major corporate announcements. Using mandatory disclosures of site visits in China, this study finds that firms receiving site visits experience higher cumulative abnormal returns before profit distribution announcements, consistent with the view that site visits transmit information to the market before formal disclosure. The incremental pricing effect of site visits, however, weakens when event signals become stronger. Investor attention further facilitates the pricing of site-visit-related information, whereas different sources of information complexity either strengthen this pricing role in high-signal payout events or weaken the general transmission of site-visit information. Further trading evidence shows that major shareholders and executives are more likely to reduce their holdings when their trading operations are preceded by high-signal payout events with prior site visits, and that mutual funds affiliated with the corresponding site-visit institutions exhibit staged holding adjustments around these events. Overall, the evidence suggests that site visits provide an observable channel through which incremental information enters prices before formal disclosure, although this pricing role varies with event signal strength and information-processing conditions.

en.takeaway: Screen for recent site visits ahead of expected payout announcements, buy pre-announcement, exit at the disclosure.

ssrn-7382222.abstract: Frequent geopolitical shocks and swings in global energy prices have strengthened cross-market connectedness and tail risk spillover among energy, equity and foreign exchange markets, which suggests that conventional static portfolio optimization may fail to adapt to intricate market conditions. This paper establishes a time-varying bi-objective portfolio optimization framework built upon the dynamic R-Vine Copula model. Empirical evidence points to notable lower-tail dependence across the three markets; the magnitude of risk spillovers appears to surge amid crisis episodes such as geopolitical clashes and global monetary tightening cycles. By embedding dynamic risk contagion channels into portfolio decision rules, the proposed model allows for adaptive weight rebalancing that seeks a trade-off between return maximization and CVaR minimization. Based on the evaluation metrics adopted in this research, the dynamic optimization strategy tends to deliver better performance relative to static specifications and equal-weighted benchmark portfolios in respect of risk-adjusted returns and downside risk containment. The present work may offer viable methodological references for constructing cross-market dynamic portfolios, and its findings could provide tentative practical insights for investors conducting multi-asset allocation and managing cross-market systemic risks.

ssrn-7382939.abstract: On declared supports containing a one-parameter family of terminal-segment curve deformations, and under the printed integrability and quote-Slater hypotheses, no finite book of caplets, floorlets, physical or cash-settled swaptions, or standard-timing CMS products on any finite strike-tenor panel bounds any superlinear moment of the annuity pricing weight: exact joint caplet-swaption calibration fails an observable well-posedness criterion. One payment-timing quote per date repairs this. The in-advance claim's price is affinely a second moment of the inverse terminal bond price, yielding a market-implied coercive gauge, a compact closed weighted-smile image, and an exact support-function dual; a single settlement family on the compounded tape carries every date's budget, while plain compounded futures provably cannot. Deterministic fixtures certify each mechanism.

en.takeaway: Add in-advance settlement quotes to the input set of any joint cap-swaption vol calibrator you build.

ssrn-7383119.abstract: A frictionless view holds that intermediaries do not affect asset prices because households alone determine valuations. A simple model of delegation shows instead that prices reflect a weighted average of households' and intermediaries' subjective beliefs, with household influence determined by delegation strength, risk attitudes, and intermediaries' regulatory and contractual incentives. We use investor surveys to recover household influence as a time-varying latent process. We reject the frictionless view even in the stock market, arguably the least intermediated major asset class, while showing that the growth of intermediation substantially overstates the dilution of household influence. We link fluctuations in influence to risk, financial constraints, and the regulatory and technological forces reshaping US markets.

bullets: Frictionless view says households alone set valuations
Delegation model: prices weight household and intermediary beliefs
Investor surveys back out household influence over time
Rejects frictionless view; intermediation overstates household dilution

en.method: A delegation model plus latent-state estimation of household influence from investor surveys.
en.one_liner: Recovers households' weight in stock prices as a time-varying latent series.
en.relevance_why: Scores 2: no trading rule, and it hinges on survey data that is hard to source and slow to update.

ssrn-7383120.abstract: Reweighting a probability law by a positive numéraire and pushing forward the payoffto-numéraire ratio yields the change-of-numéraire reweighting: the swap-rate law under the annuity measure, the numéraire-inversion involution of martingale optimal transport, and the population form of self-normalized importance sampling. We characterize exactly when it is Wasserstein-stable. Along weakly convergent inputs with uniformly integrable numéraires and a strictly positive limiting numéraire mean, convergence of the reweighted laws is equivalent to a uniform integrability condition, computed under the inputs, on one explicit family in the payoff and numéraire. At first order the numéraire cancels, the sole obstruction being payoff mass where the numéraire vanishes; absent such mass, prices and first moments pass to the limit under a uniformly integrable payoff alone, with no assumption on the reciprocal numéraire. Two-atom examples with bounded inputs attain the threshold exactly. Applications characterize a standing moment assumption in the transport literature and delimit which annuity-measure statistics survive.

bullets: Gap: limit behavior of annuity-measure laws was unspecified
Method: weak convergence plus uniformly integrable numéraires
Result: stability equals one explicit UI condition
en.data: Theory only
en.method: Proves convergence of reweighted laws is equivalent to uniform integrability of one explicit payoff-numéraire family.
en.one_liner: Pins down exactly when change-of-numéraire reweighting is Wasserstein-stable.
en.relevance_why: Score 1: pure probability theory with no signal or rule; data availability is a non-issue since it needs none, but there is nothing to automate.
en.takeaway: Use it as a sanity check on self-normalized importance sampling and annuity-measure estimators before trusting them.

ssrn-7383378.abstract: I study returns to leveraged single stock ETFs (LSS-ETFs), decomposing the return shortfall relative to a simple benchmark into a component attributable to daily rebalancing trades and one attributable to frictions such as fees, trading costs, and excess loan margins. For my main sample comprised of thirty-five ETFs introduced since June 2022, LSS-ETFs underperform by an average of 0.75% per month, with 0.20% attributable to daily rebalancing and 0.55% to frictions. For a supplemental sample of 235 ETFs listed since April 2024 long levered single stock ETFs underperform by an average of 1.47% per month, with 0.42% attributable to daily rebalancing and 1.04% to frictions. Consistent with theory, rebalancing costs are negatively related to return serial correlation as captured by return variance ratios and positively related to daily volatility. Analysis of a broader sample of hypothetical single-stock ETF returns over the past fifty years reveals that LSS-ETFs underperform on average when return volatility is high, not due to volatility per se, but because high volatility periods are characterized by return reversals. Some results reported here are extracted from a prior working paper titled "Returns to Constant Leverage Strategies: General Principles and Application to Levered Single-Stock ETFs."

bullets: Prior work lumps levered ETF decay into one unexplained drag
He decomposes the shortfall into rebalancing and friction parts
35 ETFs lag 0.75%/month: 0.20% rebalancing, 0.55% frictions
Reversals, not volatility itself, drive losses in high-vol regimes
en.data: 35 LSS-ETFs listed since June 2022, 235 listed since April 2024, plus 50 years of hypothetical single-stock ETF returns.
en.method: Return decomposition against a constant-leverage benchmark, with rebalancing cost regressed on variance ratios and daily volatility.
en.one_liner: Bessembinder splits levered single-stock ETF underperformance into rebalancing drag and frictions.
en.relevance_why: Score 4: prices and listing dates are free and standard, and the rule tells you which popular products not to hold, though borrow availability is left to the implementer.
en.takeaway: Screen out long levered ETFs on low-variance-ratio, high-volatility names; harvest the 1.47%/month drag by shorting them or replicating with the underlying.

ssrn-7383518.abstract: Financial regulators promote open data to dismantle monopolies and improve transparency. Yet financial data feeds bundle two distinct objects: information about fundamentals and about liquidity demand. In a strategic-trading model with an upstream data market, competition among data vendors broadens fundamental access and sharpens price discovery, but also induces them to disseminate order-flow signals. These reveal no fundamentals but make liquidity demand predictable, raising market makers' price impact. Hence an open-data paradox: competition can make prices more informative yet markets less liquid. We characterize an information-design remedy, selective openness: broad fundamental access with restricted order-flow data.

en.takeaway: Use it to argue which way execution-cost assumptions should move if data-access rules change.

ssrn-7383518.title: Open Data, Order-Flow Privacy, and Market Quality

ssrn-7383698.abstract: Why does relationship-based voice trade remain dominant in the U.S. corporate bond interdealer market despite lower-friction electronic alternatives, and is this market structure efficient? Using transaction-level data, we show that dealers increasingly choose voice venue when inventory imbalances make immediacy valuable, because voice venue provides access to established trading relationships. Voice execution is slower than electronic execution for micro trades but faster for orders of at least $100,000, which account for nearly all interdealer par volume. We develop and calibrate a searchand-matching model where dealers choose trading venues contingent on their inventory balances. Voice venue offers two advantages: on average dealers meet counterparties faster, and because dealers with large imbalances sort into the voice venue, they meet better counterparties, whose positions are more likely to offset their own. The endogenous second channel accounts for roughly three quarters of the voice venue's advantage in the calibrated model. In equilibrium, voice venues are valuable but inefficiently allocated and overused by dealers with limited need for immediacy. A social planner retains the most imbalanced dealers in voice but reallocates near-target dealers to electronic trading, reducing the share of dealers searching in voice from 72% to 25%.
ssrn-7383698.affiliations: Tsinghua University - Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management, CMU Tepper School of Business and Tsinghua University, SEM

en.takeaway: When routing large corporate bond orders under a big inventory imbalance, check voice execution speed before defaulting to electronic.

ssrn-7383698.title: Why Voice Trading Persists: The Value of Interdealer Relationships

ssrn-7383998.abstract: In 2026, U.S. options markets went through three changes at roughly the same time: FINRA eliminated the Pattern Day Trader (PDT) rule and its $25,000 minimum-equity threshold (effective June 4, 2026); zero-daysto-expiration (0DTE) options kept growing, reaching a record 66.2% of S&P 500 index options volume by July; and Cboe completed a near-24-hour trading window covering SPX, VIX, Mini-SPX, and Russell 2000 index options. Using Cboe's own investor disclosures, this paper documents that all three changes are described to investors primarily in terms of engagement and volume growth, while retail-facing communications about the same events emphasize flexibility and access. This paper does not claim that any entity intended to harm retail traders, nor does it establish a causal link between these friction removals and retail trading losses. What it documents is an observable asymmetry in how the commercial value of these changes is communicated to different audiences. Combined with well-established findings that most retail options buyers lose money and that traders routinely fail to exit at planned loss levels, this asymmetry points to a gap in current disclosure regimes. The paper proposes a voluntary, opt-in risk control feature-a platform-level button, available inside any retail trading app, that traders can turn on or off at will-which, once activated, locks a trader's selfdefined loss threshold in place for a set period. Rooted in behavioral-economics commitment-device theory, it holds traders to their own stated risk plan at the moment when research predicts they are most likely to abandon it. AI is proposed as implementation infrastructure for this feature, not as the theoretical contribution.

Reads Cboe's investor vs retail disclosures side by side
Same events sold as volume growth, then as access

en.method: Qualitative comparison of Cboe disclosure language, plus a commitment-device design grounded in behavioral economics.

en.takeaway: No tradable signal — useful only as background on the PDT repeal (June 4, 2026) and 0DTE at 66.2% of SPX volume when modeling retail flow.

ssrn-7383998.title: Frictionless Losses: Deregulation, Exchange Incentives, and a Case for Platform-Level Risk Controls in Retail Options Markets

ssrn-7384158.abstract: Bolivia possesses approximately 22% of identified global lithium resources-one of the world's largest endowments-yet in 2025 produced just 2,400 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent, less than 1% of South American output. This paper demonstrates that Bolivia's production gap is primarily institutional: a bilateral monopoly with Chinese and Russian state-owned enterprises has trapped the sovereign in a low-BATNA equilibrium, enabling counterparties to capture quasi-rents through opaque pricing and one-sided risk allocation. We propose Commodity-Linked Participation Rights (CLPRs), an exchange-cleared security that transforms Bolivia's bargaining structure from bilateral negotiation to a "negotiauction"-a hybrid mechanism in which competitive bidding determines price while negotiated governance provisions preserve sovereign discretion. Drawing on Subramanian's negotiauction theory and Acemoglu and Robinson's institutional economics framework, we develop a formal bargaining model in which the credible availability of a CLPR auction improves the sovereign's outside option, altering the equilibrium terms of bilateral resource negotiations. Under our baseline parameterisation, the simulated effective financing cost falls from an implicit 12%+ to approximately 7.4%, with the probability of payment distress declining from 35% to 8.2%. The framework generalises to other resource-rich developing economies facing sovereignty-financing trade-offs.

Introduces Commodity-Linked Participation Rights, auctioned and cleared

en.data: Theory only — results come from a baseline parameterisation, not historical data.
en.method: A formal bargaining model built on Subramanian's negotiauction theory and Acemoglu-Robinson institutional economics.
en.one_liner: Proposes an exchange-cleared security to strengthen Bolivia's lithium bargaining position.
en.relevance_why: Policy and institutional design with no automatable rules, and CLPRs do not exist yet, so no price data can be sourced.
en.takeaway: Background reading for lithium supply forecasts or sovereign credit views, not a tradable signal.

ssrn-7384259.abstract: Power-plus valuation gives an elementary one-period option pricing formula and an explicit recursion under repeated application. We study when this algebraically prescribed recursion also admits a dynamically coherent multi-period martingale stopping representation. The key restriction is recursive. Whenever the holder continues at a successor state, that state must itself support the remaining prescribed recursion. For a stylized convertible claim, we solve this backward feasibility problem exactly. With n ≥ 2 future conversion dates, the viable states form the finite half-open interval D_n = [0, d_n), where d_n is the exact viability boundary. These boundaries contract strictly as the number of remaining conversion dates increases. Once finite exercise states disappear, recursive viability becomes strictly more restrictive than the ordinary one-step martingale bound. We construct finite-support Borel Markov kernels that realize the prescribed stopping values throughout the viable domains for each fixed contract. Finally, under dense conversion grids we identify a sharp phase transition. Depending on the relative scaling of the power parameter and the grid spacing, the issuance viability boundary either converges to a finite limit or diverges.
ssrn-7384259.affiliations: and New York University (NYU) - Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences

Method: solve backward feasibility for a convertible claim
Result: viable states shrink to [0, d_n) for n >= 2 dates
Dense grids give a sharp converge-or-diverge transition

en.takeaway: Use it as a sanity check on convertible-style pricing recursions: flag states where the recursion has no arbitrage-free stopping representation.

ssrn-7384278.abstract: The non-Gaussian CAPM states that beta and coskewness are the only two systematic risks: beta captures second-order risk, while coskewness captures third-order risk. However, the empirical performance of coskewness is known to be weak. Using a return-moment expansion, I decompose coskewness into a sum of correlations between stock and market moments. If investors care less about higher-order risks, these components should receive unequal prices. In Fama-MacBeth regressions of individual stocks excluding microcaps, only the lowest-order component, the variance-variance correlation, earns a significant premium; higher-order cross-moment correlations do not. Thus, third-order risk is priced, but in a more nuanced way. A strategy combining beta and the variance-variance correlation earns about 9% annually, unexplained by Fama-French factors.

bullets: Coskewness is theoretically a systematic risk but empirically weak
A return-moment expansion breaks it into stock-market correlations
Fama-MacBeth on non-microcaps prices only the lowest-order term
Beta plus variance-variance correlation returns ~9% a year
en.data: Cross-section of individual US-style stock returns excluding microcaps; the abstract gives no sample window.
en.method: The author expands returns in moments, decomposes coskewness into correlations between stock and market moments, then prices each component separately.
en.one_liner: Splitting coskewness shows only its variance-variance part is priced.
en.relevance_why: Score 4: daily returns are all you need to compute the moments, but rebalancing cadence and portfolio construction are left open.
en.takeaway: Build a variance-variance correlation factor from daily returns and pair it with beta in a long-short book.

ssrn-7384278.title: Another Moment for CAPM

ssrn-7384279.abstract: This paper studies whether fintech innovation can relax short-sale constraints and improve price discovery. I examine Robinhood's May 2022 stock lending program, which mobilized dispersed retail shareholdings into the securities-lending market. Using a difference-indifferences design, I find evidence that the program relaxes short-sale constraints for stocks heavily owned by retail investors. Short interest rises by 0.43 percentage points among stocks more exposed to the program. Further evidence suggests that Robinhood helps bring retail-held shares into the lending market, increasing lendable supply outside the traditional institutional lending pool. I also find suggestive evidence of improved price discovery: anomaly-related pricing errors decline more among stocks exposed to the program, with larger declines on the short than on the long side for several anomalies. Overall, the evidence suggests that fintech innovation can relax limits to arbitrage and improve price discovery by making dispersed shareholdings easier to intermediate into the securities-lending market.

bullets: Retail shares sit idle, outside the institutional lending pool
Difference-in-differences around the May 2022 program launch
Short interest rose 0.43pp for high-exposure stocks
Anomaly pricing errors fell more, mostly on the short side

en.method: Difference-in-differences comparing stocks by exposure to the Robinhood lending program.
en.one_liner: Tests whether Robinhood's stock lending program loosened short-sale constraints.

ssrn-7384279.title: Fintech Innovation, Short Selling, and Market Efficiency

ssrn-7384638.abstract: Indonesia's benchmark equity index is dominated by two large-capitalization clusters that respond to structurally different macroeconomic drivers: systemically important banks (BBCA, BMRI, BBNI, BBRI), whose valuations are primarily a function of the domestic credit cycle and Bank Indonesia's policy rate, and high-payout thermal coal exporters (ITMG, BSSR), whose earnings and dividends track the US-dollar-denominated Newcastle coal benchmark, a price series subject to boom-bust supercycle dynamics driven by Chinese and Indian demand, weather, and geopolitics. Because these two return-generating mechanisms are largely independent of one another over multi-year horizons, and because each has historically produced identifiable, if noisy, turning-point signals — a peaking-and-pausing policy rate for banks, and a price approaching the marginal cost of production for coal — this paper argues that a regime-conditional rotation strategy between the two clusters is more defensible, on both diversification and timing grounds, than a static buy-and-hold allocation to either. Drawing on the bank interest-rate-sensitivity literature (Flannery & James, 1984; English, Van den Heuvel, & Zakrajšek, 2018), the commodity supercycle literature (Jacks, 2019; Erten & Ocampo, 2013), the dividend-signaling literature (Fama & French, 1988; Michaely, Thaler, & Womack, 1995), and the sector-rotation literature (Conover, Jensen, Johnson, & Mercer, 2008), this paper develops a two-axis regime matrix — policy-rate direction against commodity-price-forecast direction — together with a four-stage barbell rotation checklist for moving capital between the two clusters. A fifteen-year historical mapping of the Indonesian market (2011–2026) illustrates the framework's internal consistency, and the framework is applied to conditions prevailing in August 2026, in which Bank Indonesia's policy rate had just entered a pause after a cumulative 100-basis-point tightening cycle while Newcastle coal remained priced above its own three-year-forward consensus, as an exploratory case illustration. An agenda for controlled backtesting against a monetary-conditions rotation benchmark and a time-series-momentum benchmark is proposed.

bullets: Banks track the credit cycle; coal miners track Newcastle prices
The two return drivers stay independent over multi-year horizons
Two-axis matrix: policy-rate direction vs coal-price forecast
2011-2026 mapping plus an Aug 2026 case; no backtest yet
en.data: Four Indonesian banks (BBCA, BMRI, BBNI, BBRI), two coal exporters (ITMG, BSSR), Newcastle coal prices and the Bank Indonesia policy rate, mapped over 2011-2026. Controlled backtesting is only proposed, not run.
en.method: A two-axis regime matrix (policy-rate direction against commodity-price-forecast direction) plus a four-stage barbell rotation checklist.
en.one_liner: Proposes a regime-conditional rotation between Indonesian banks and coal miners.
en.relevance_why: Score 2: rules stay checklist-level with no backtest, and while prices and the BI rate are public, the three-year-forward coal consensus and marginal-cost estimates sit behind paid data.
en.takeaway: Build regime flags from BI rate peaks/pauses and spot coal versus its forward curve to tilt Indonesian sector exposure.

ssrn-7384719.abstract: Factor models conventionally form portfolios annually using stale financial statements released months earlier. We construct fresh factors each month using the most recent annual financial statements. Fresh factors modestly improve pricing, but augmenting the stale model with the change in returns from updating stale portfolio assignments significantly improves pricing because the two components carry different pricing content. This reallocates abnormal returns, reverses the interpretation of thousands of event-study CARs, and reclassifies 14.7% of top-decile mutual funds. These findings reveal a fundamental structure in returns: a slow-moving component reflecting persistent fundamental risk and a fast-moving component capturing the arrival of information.
ssrn-7384719.affiliations: Mays Business School at Texas A&M University, University of North Carolina Kenan-Flagler Business School, University of Utah - Department of Finance and Brigham Young University
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Standard factors rebalance annually on financial statements months old
Authors rebuild factors monthly from the latest annual statements
Fresh factors help a little; adding the update-induced return change helps a lot
Reverses thousands of event-study CARs, reclassifies 14.7% of top-decile funds
en.data: US firm financial statements and returns, event-study CARs, and mutual fund performance; the abstract gives no sample window.
en.method: Monthly factor reconstruction from the most recent annual statements, plus a second factor for the return change from reassigning stale portfolios.
en.one_liner: Split factors into a stale fundamental component and a monthly-refresh component to price returns better.
en.relevance_why: Score 4: reproducible from Compustat and CRSP, both standard, but entry/exit rules and universe are left to you.
en.takeaway: Use the two-component benchmark to attribute alpha and screen managers whose edge is just stale-factor drift.

bullets: 기존 팩터는 몇 달 전 재무제표로 1년에 한 번만 포트폴리오를 짠다

ssrn-7384838.abstract: Institutional investors commonly separate strategic asset allocation (SAA) from tactical asset allocation (TAA). This governance structure is practical, but repeated one-period tactical optimization can be dynamically suboptimal when positions persist, signals evolve, and changing exposure is costly. We develop a discrete-time benchmark-relative model with an evolving strategic reference, tactical return predictors, quadratic trading costs, and a discounted recursive entropic criterion for continuation-value uncertainty. The optimal policy trades partially toward a forward-looking dynamic aim portfolio. In a scalar benchmark, we derive an exact persistence threshold separating attenuation from amplification of current tactical signals relative to one-period TAA. In a transitory-predictor setting, greater uncertainty about future predictor realizations reduces the signal-driven aim but increases the adjustment rate toward it, lowering the net current signal response. We also characterize trading-cost effects, obtaining general multivariate value and action-penalty orderings and sharper directional policy results in scalar or aligned settings. We distinguish one-step action loss from the full recursive loss generated by repeatedly following a suboptimal policy, derive exact fixed-policy and policy-loss identities, and use them to choose the best rule within a restricted, governance-compatible two-step SAA-TAA family. Numerical illustrations show that value-based calibration can materially improve a simple institutional rule even when coefficient proximity to the dynamic optimum is a poor guide to economic performance.
ssrn-7384838.affiliations: and New York University (NYU) - Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences

bullets: Repeated one-period TAA is dynamically suboptimal
Discrete-time model with quadratic costs, entropic criterion
Persistence threshold splits signal amplification from attenuation
en.data: Theory only; numerical illustrations, no empirical dataset.
en.method: Benchmark-relative discrete-time control with an evolving strategic reference, quadratic trading costs and a discounted recursive entropic criterion; the optimum trades partially toward a forward-looking aim portfolio.
en.one_liner: Kolm and Ritter solve dynamic SAA-TAA allocation with costs and predictable returns.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: the policy is implementable from standard price data, but you must estimate predictors and costs and design the calibration yourself.
en.takeaway: Set tactical signal scaling and rebalance speed from signal persistence and cost estimates instead of re-solving each period.

ssrn-7385238.abstract: Kelly, Malamud and Zhou (2024, KMZ) show that highly complex prediction models can outperform simple ones when forecasting U.S. stock returns. We test this claim in two settings: the South African stock market, a smaller emerging market, and a shorter, more recent U.S. window (2017-2025) than KMZ's original sample, using the same random-feature ridge machine and ten simple benchmarks. Under KMZ's short-window design, accuracy in both countries rises with model complexity, as their theory predicts. Under a longer, more realistic window that includes trading costs and compares against the strongest simple alternative, however, the complex machine underperforms in both markets, losing to three simple models in South Africa and to the historical mean and a shrunk ridge regression in the United States. Placebo tests indicate the signal is genuine rather than spurious, but a large part of it traces to a single momentum variable, and accuracy deteriorates sharply once predictors are moderately noisy. A weaker version of the same pattern appears even in the developed market that motivated the original theory.
ssrn-7385238.affiliations: Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science - Stellenbosch University and Stellenbosch University
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

Same random-feature ridge machine versus ten simple benchmarks

ssrn-7385238.title: The Complexity Mirage

ssrn-7385740.abstract: Market commentary often compresses a rise in Japanese government bond yields into a single causal chain: yen funding becomes more expensive, carry trades unwind, and global risk assets reprice. This paper tests the empirical content of that label. Using daily Japanese yield-curve innovations, a 12-currency exposure panel, and a separately constructed non-yen high-minus-low carry factor from 2013 through July 2026, the design separates short-end from long-duration shocks, positive from negative repricing, and high-from normal-volatility states. The carry-unwind signature is sharply conditional. In the currency panel, positive short-end shocks produce a stronger five-day loss gradient among economies with larger predetermined yen-credit exposure only in high-volatility states; the interaction survives Holm correction (p = 0.018), and the positive-minus-negative high-volatility contrast also survives (p = 0.010). In the separately constructed carry factor, the total slope on positive short-end repricing is negative at one and five days in high-volatility states, with Holm-adjusted p-values of 0.016 and 0.018. Negative short-end and long-duration shocks are close to zero. Event paths are directionally consistent but weaker: funding-type shocks are followed by a 1.51% twenty-day carry loss versus 0.31% after duration-type shocks, with a suggestive difference (p = 0.064). A 90th-percentile volatility threshold and release-lag checks preserve the main ordering. The evidence supports a state-contingent classification, not a generic causal claim: carry unwind is not a synonym for rising JGB yields.

bullets: Tests the 'JGB yields up = carry unwind' shorthand directly
Splits short-end vs long-duration, up vs down, vol states
Only positive short-end shocks bite: Holm p=0.018
en.data: Daily Japanese yield-curve innovations, a 12-currency exposure panel, and a separately built non-yen high-minus-low carry factor, 2013 through July 2026.
en.method: Regresses daily Japanese curve innovations, split by tenor and sign, on currency-panel returns and a carry factor, interacted with volatility state and Holm-corrected.
en.one_liner: Rising JGB yields unwind carry only in high-volatility states.
en.relevance_why: Yields, FX and vol are all standard public data, but the paper gives conditions rather than entry/exit rules, so you still design the strategy.
en.takeaway: Use it as a risk filter: cut carry exposure on positive short-end JGB shocks in high-vol states, ignore duration and negative shocks.

ssrn-7385778.abstract: Transport is undergoing its greatest transformation since the horse carriage gave way to the motor car: in 2025 one in four new cars sold worldwide was electric, driverless taxis complete roughly half a million paid rides a week in American metropolitan areas, and software is turning the vehicle from a product of mechanical craftsmanship into a computer on wheels. This paper-the first of six devoted to the great megatrends-orders the field of future mobility along its five arenas: decarbonisation and alternative drive systems, autonomous driving, connectivity, shared mobility, and the urban transformation including micromobility. The paper examines market positions and timetables: battery prices have fallen by more than 90 per cent since 2010 (2025: USD 108 per kilowatt-hour), five-minute charging is series production reality in China, driverless lorries have been running in Texas since 2025, and the robotaxi market could grow to more than USD 400 billion by 2035 — while the privately owned Level 4 car is, by broad agreement, unlikely before the 2030s and will dominate the vehicle fleet only decades later. For investors, the paper names listed companies along the entire value chain — large and mid caps exclusively — with their business ideas and trading venues, and identifies two ETFs that pass the selection checklist developed in the text. The investment conclusion cuts both ways: the megatrend is real, but its returns are unevenly distributed and have historically flowed to the suppliers of scarce key technology rather than to the car brands. Thematic ETFs launched near peak sentiment have lost roughly 30 per cent in risk-adjusted terms over their first five years. Whoever wants to take part therefore diversifies across the value chain, weights platform and technology leaders above hopeful newcomers, avoids naming small specialists, and measures success in decades, not quarters.

Splits mobility into five arenas, from EVs to micromobility
2025: 1 in 4 new cars electric; batteries at USD 108/kWh
Returns went to scarce-technology suppliers, not car brands
en.data: Theory only
en.method: Narrative survey plus a hand-built selection checklist applied to large and mid caps and two ETFs.
en.one_liner: A survey of the future-mobility megatrend and where investors can buy into it.
en.relevance_why: Score 1: no signal, no rules, no backtest — an investment survey. Its numbers (battery prices, robotaxi ride counts, the USD 400bn 2035 forecast) are public but scattered, so even building the feature set means assembling data by hand.
en.takeaway: Use it as a starting universe and value-chain taxonomy; the trading rules are yours to write.

ssrn-7385839.abstract: A frictionless view holds that intermediaries do not affect asset prices because households alone determine valuations. A simple model of delegation shows instead that prices reflect a weighted average of households' and intermediaries' subjective beliefs, with household influence determined by delegation strength, risk attitudes, and intermediaries' regulatory and contractual incentives. We use investor surveys to recover household influence as a time-varying latent process. We reject the frictionless view even in the stock market, arguably the least intermediated major asset class, while showing that the growth of intermediation substantially overstates the dilution of household influence. We link fluctuations in influence to risk, financial constraints, and the regulatory and technological forces reshaping US markets.

bullets: Tests the frictionless view that only households set prices
Delegation model: prices weight household and intermediary beliefs
Investor surveys back out household influence over time
Frictionless view rejected even in equities
en.data: US investor surveys and intermediation measures; the abstract gives no sample window.
en.method: A delegation model plus investor surveys, estimated as a latent time-varying influence process.
en.one_liner: The authors recover households' price-setting influence as a time-varying latent process.
en.relevance_why: Score 2: survey-based latent estimates are hard to source and replicate, and no entry or exit rules are given.
en.takeaway: Use the influence series as a macro regime filter tied to risk and funding constraints.

ssrn-7385839.title: Household Influence in the Stock Market: A Belief-based Approach

ssrn-7385978.abstract: A frictionless view holds that intermediaries do not affect asset prices because households alone determine valuations. A simple model of delegation shows instead that prices reflect a weighted average of households' and intermediaries' subjective beliefs, with household influence determined by delegation strength, risk attitudes, and intermediaries' regulatory and contractual incentives. We use investor surveys to recover household influence as a time-varying latent process. We reject the frictionless view even in the stock market, arguably the least intermediated major asset class, while showing that the growth of intermediation substantially overstates the dilution of household influence. We link fluctuations in influence to risk, financial constraints, and the regulatory and technological forces reshaping US markets.

bullets: Targets the claim that intermediaries never move prices
Delegation model: price = weighted average of both beliefs
Investor surveys back out influence as a latent time series
Rejects frictionless view; intermediation growth overstates dilution
en.data: US investor sentiment surveys; the abstract names no sample window.
en.method: A delegation equilibrium model, with investor surveys used to estimate household influence as a time-varying latent process.
en.one_liner: Surveys recover household pricing influence and reject the frictionless view.
en.relevance_why: Scored 2 because it explains price formation rather than giving trade rules, and it needs survey microdata plus a custom latent-state estimation to reproduce.
en.takeaway: Use the estimated influence series as a regime filter that scales sentiment- or valuation-gap signals.

ssrn-7388478.abstract: Business Development Companies (BDCs) combine periodic reporting of illiquid private credit with continuously traded equity, providing a unique setting to evaluate private credit performance. During periods of credit stress, performance drops and stock-to-NAV discounts widen sharply as stock prices fall faster than reported NAVs. Market discounts and pre-announcement stock returns predict subsequent NAV markdowns and weaker profitability, although their predictive power is limited for larger BDCs and those with more diversified portfolios. Crucially, market metrics have limited ability to anticipate discrete distress events such as non-accruals and payment-in-kind (PIK) amendments. We find that quarterly NAV announcements contain significant, value-relevant incremental information that results in immediate stock price reactions.

Signals miss non-accruals and PIK amendments

ssrn-7389238.abstract: In equity markets characterized by double-sided statutory transaction taxation-such as India's Securities Transaction Tax (STT), state stamp duties, and exchange levies-marginal rank turnover at portfolio inclusion boundaries imposes a persistent frictional drag on crosssectional factor strategies. In a conventional monthly momentum strategy selecting the top N = 30 equities, replacing rank N + 1 with rank N incurs two full execution fee legs (≈ 42.34 bps round-trip) to capture a momentum-score differential that is frequently negligible. We formalize and evaluate an asymmetric Hysteresis Rebalancing (Banded) framework on the Indian Nifty 500 universe using point-in-time constituent data from January 2018 through February 2026, with a primary out-of-sample evaluation period from January 2021 through December 2025 (T = 1, 260 contiguous out-of-sample trading days, evaluated over a 10-fold rolling-origin walk-forward protocol). Under this regime, new entrants must achieve a strict top N = 30 momentum rank, whereas incumbent holdings are retained as long as their score remains within an exploratory upper retention buffer (R t (i) ≤ B, for B ∈ {40, 45, 50, 60}). At B = 60, monthly position churn drops by 51.7% (from 9.57 to 4.62 stocks replaced per month), while net after-cost compound annual growth rate (CAGR) improves from 41.70% to 45.12% and the Sharpe ratio rises from 1.728 to 1.849, with maximum drawdown contracting from-26.44% to-25.41%. Although paired stationary bootstrap testing indicates that the after-cost Sharpe gain (∆Sharpe = +0.121, 95% CI [-0.048, +0.310], p = 0.167) is not statistically distinguishable from zero at conventional significance levels, the observed 51.7% reduction in position churn provides evidence that hysteresis banding can materially reduce execution burden in tax-intensive equity markets.

bullets: India's STT and levies cost 42.34 bps round-trip per swap
Boundary rank swaps pay full fees for tiny score gaps
Entrants need rank 30; incumbents held to rank 60
Churn 9.57 to 4.62 names/month; net CAGR 41.70% to 45.12%
en.data: Nifty 500 point-in-time constituents, Jan 2018 to Feb 2026, with 1,260 out-of-sample days (2021-2025) under 10-fold rolling-origin walk-forward.
en.method: Asymmetric hysteresis banding: strict top-30 entry, retention buffer at B in {40, 45, 50, 60}.
en.one_liner: A retention band on a top-30 momentum portfolio halves turnover and lifts net returns.
en.relevance_why: Rules are fully specified and need only index membership and daily prices, but point-in-time Nifty 500 constituents require a paid vendor feed.
en.takeaway: Split entry and exit thresholds in any factor book where statutory taxes make rank churn expensive.

ssrn-7389258.abstract: Financial direction prediction is difficult because return distributions are non-stationary, crossasset relationships drift across regimes, and modern classifiers can be substantially overconfident. This paper documents HPT-DTE, a hybrid architecture that combines a time-domain neural sequence encoder, an FFT-based frequency-domain branch, decision-tree regime conditioning, a logistic meta-learner, and held-out isotonic calibration. For an asset, a 20-day window of twelve backward-looking technical and macroeconomic features is transformed into two representations. Time tokens receive a learnable phase-shift tensor, while real and imaginary FFT coefficients provide a harmonic representation. Multi-head cross-attention uses the time branch as query and the frequency branch as key/value; a learned sigmoid gate controls the harmonic residual. A shallow regime tree supplies a one-hot leaf condition, and an equity tree contributes an independent probability to a regularized meta-learner. The calibrated probability is converted into a selective decision with an abstention band. The reported experiment trains on nine equities during 2017-2023 and evaluates without fine-tuning on four unseen equities, three cryptocurrencies, and GLD during 2024-2026. The selective accuracy is 60.0% on TSLA and 51.4-53.6% on the three cryptocurrencies, with 22-46 predictions among 80 evaluation opportunities per asset. We provide mathematical descriptions, proofs of the calibration and selectivity properties, implementationgrounded interpretation, and a candid audit of limitations, including the distinction between trade-conditioned accuracy and unconditional forecasting accuracy.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

en.data: Trains on nine equities, 2017-2023, using 20-day windows of twelve technical and macro features; evaluates zero-shot on four unseen equities, three cryptos and GLD over 2024-2026.

en.one_liner: A time-plus-frequency classifier predicts asset direction and abstains when unsure.

en.takeaway: Borrow the calibration-plus-abstention layer as an entry filter on top of your existing direction signals.

ssrn-7389261.abstract: Does an unanticipated change in U.S. monetary policy raise the yield on Australian Government Securities, and with it the cost of Australian government borrowing? We show that the answer depends critically on when one asks it. Using the high-frequency shock series of Jarociński and Karadi (2020) and Local Projections across the 2-, 5-, and 10-year AGS maturities over 2013-2024, we find the effect is statistically indistinguishable from zero before 2020, and becomes large and reliable only from the COVID period onward-a shift confirmed by a formal structural break test. A surprise comparable to the largest observed in our sample is associated with an increase of approximately eighteen to twenty basis points in Australian yields at impact, operating substantially through co-movement in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield. These findings indicate that Australian government borrowing costs have grown considerably more exposed to U.S. monetary policy surprises specifically in the post-2020 environment.

bullets: Tests whether Fed surprises spill into AGS yields
Local projections on high-frequency policy shocks
Pre-2020 effect is indistinguishable from zero
Largest-sample surprise adds ~18-20bp on impact
en.data: AGS 2y/5y/10y yields, U.S. 10-year Treasury yields, and FOMC high-frequency shocks, 2013-2024.
en.method: Local projections of 2-, 5-, and 10-year AGS yields on Jarocinski-Karadi (2020) high-frequency shocks, with a formal structural break test.
en.one_liner: U.S. policy surprises move Australian government yields only after 2020.
en.relevance_why: It is a macro spillover result, not a rule; the shock series comes from an authors' dataset that updates with a lag.
en.takeaway: Size AGS duration risk around FOMC dates, routed through the U.S. 10-year, in the post-2020 regime.

ssrn-7390378.abstract: This paper specifies a Layer-1 blockchain protocol whose monetary issuance is mechanically indexed to the network's verifiable operating cost plus a small, bounded margin. New tokens are minted only to the extent required to cover attested energy, compute, and infrastructure expenditure incurred in processing and finalizing blocks, and to fund a stability buffer. The design objective is a cryptoasset whose issuance adjusts to verified operating cost and prevailing token value, limiting cumulative dilution and dampening price volatility over time without reliance on fiat reserves. This revision incorporates a significant development in market infrastructure: the emergence of independent GPU rental-rate benchmarks and exchange-listed compute derivatives, which supply the protocol with regulated, market-settled reference rates for its cost oracle and permit hedging of the protocol's cost base. We present the issuance rule, admissible cost basis, attestation architecture, oracle design, fee and buffer mechanics, consensus model, threat model, governance, and institutional use cases for real-world-asset (RWA) tokenization and settlement.

bullets: Stabilizing a cryptoasset without fiat reserves remains unsolved
Issuance covers attested energy, compute and infrastructure spend
GPU rental benchmarks and listed compute derivatives feed the oracle
Paper covers attestation, fees, buffer, consensus, governance, RWA use

en.method: A protocol spec: issuance rule, admissible cost basis, attestation architecture, oracle design, consensus and threat model.
en.one_liner: Specifies a Layer-1 protocol that mints tokens only up to verified operating cost plus a bounded margin.
en.relevance_why: Score 1 — a design document with no signal, no backtest and no tradable asset, and the GPU-rate and compute-derivative data it relies on sit in a nascent market that is hard to source.
en.takeaway: Nothing to trade today; if compute derivatives list, track their settled rates as a mining-cost input for crypto valuation.

ssrn-7390378.title: Cost-Indexed Crypto: A Framework for Volatility-Dampening Monetary Issuance Through Verifiable Operating Costs and Exchange-Settled Compute Benchmarks

ssrn-7390420.abstract: No technology has ever moved so much capital in so little time: the four large cloud groups plan to invest around USD 735 billion in 2026 — more than five times their 2023 outlay —, NVIDIA's data-centre business approaches USD 200 billion in annual revenue, and the model providers OpenAI and Anthropic report annualised revenues of more than 40 and 65 billion US dollars respectively. This paper — the second of six on the great megatrends — classifies artificial intelligence as a general purpose technology, maps its value chain from chips through data centres and models to applications, and tests the bubble question against hard numbers. The empirical picture cuts both ways. On the one hand, controlled studies document sizeable productivity gains — 15 per cent in customer service, 40 per cent time saved in writing tasks, 56 per cent faster programming — and the investments are largely paid out of the current profits of the world's most profitable companies. On the other hand, index concentration has reached historic highs — the ten largest US names make up more than 40 per cent of the S&P 500, more than at the peak of the dotcom bubble —, circular financing between chip makers, cloud providers and model firms is growing, and according to a widely discussed MIT study 95 per cent of corporate pilot projects have yet to deliver a measurable profit contribution. For investors, the paper names listed companies along the entire chain — exclusively large and mid caps, with business idea and trading venues — and applies the fixed ETF checklist: physical replication, fund size of at least EUR 0.2 billion, sustainability classification, costs, the currency question, issuer, UCITS framework and exchange trading. The most important single lesson: whoever holds a world index already owns roughly a third of the AI complex through its heavyweights — every additional position is a deliberate overweight and should be sized accordingly.
